purpose: The first application code in this repository. RFC-2026-015 closed DATA-DEC-01 (`app`) and DATA-DEC-02 (a wrapper command contract, no tool named), which is exactly what the data package says gates the DB-00 merge and the start of DB-00 coding. This increment lands the batch 000 migration, the deterministic command contract, and the half of the schema lint decidable from the repository. The half needing a live Postgres is wired to REFUSE: this host has no psql, pg_ctl or docker and the repository forbids adding a dependency, so a harness that printed a pass would be the largest false clean run this repository has produced -- on the one surface where a false pass means tenant data.

acceptance_criteria: Batch 000 creates the app and private schemas with DATA-DEC-01's approved name, grants nothing to a client role, and touches no Supabase-managed schema.
Every target the data package names is reachable through make, sets LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC, and prints a stable summary line whether it passes or fails.
Every target needing a database exits non-zero without one and names DB_TEST_URL. None reports a pass it cannot earn.
A connection string never reaches stdout or stderr.
Each schema lint rule is shown to REJECT a violating input, not merely to pass batch 000.
The lint rejects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY without FORCE, which the lint rule the data package specifies would pass.
npm run check stays green with no test skipped and no declared floor lowered.
Batch 132 creates no table, view, function, policy or grant, and the migration set is the source of that claim rather than a regex written beside it.

The measurement behind the refusal is falsifiable: the two keys an effective limit would join are shown to live in different migrations, the fixtures are shown to intersect in nothing, and each of batch 061's four open questions is quoted from batch 061 and named as needed.

open_blockers:
BATCH 110 STORES NO PROVIDER TOKEN, AND THE DECISION IS BATCH 060's FOLLOWED RATHER THAN REMADE. A connector holds OAuth tokens and §9.1 gives "OAuth token" as its own example of `SECRET-4`, whose storage rule is "vault/encrypted secret store; NEVER PLAINTEXT DB/LOG". Five sources agree and none of them is this batch: §9.2's absolute prohibitions name "plaintext BYOK/API key/OAuth access token/refresh token/webhook secret" and fix a secret table's permitted column list exhaustively; §4 invariant 9 says a credential is stored as a secret reference only and not in an exposed row; §3.1 puts "secret references" in `private` with no direct grant; §14's G0 checklist requires a secret table not be exposed; and §8.3's "Plain credential SELECT" is `N` for every role including the service.

So private.meta_credential_references is batch 060's private.ai_credential_references for a Meta connection, statement for statement: a LOCATOR in the vault, §9.2's column list enforced as an APPLY-TIME ALLOWLIST so a later batch adding `access_token text` fails the MIGRATION rather than the code review, a sixteen-character ceiling on the fingerprint so a whole token does not fit, and NO GRANT TO ANY ROLE. Two differences are declared rather than left for a reviewer to find: no `provider` column (§9.2 permits one and 060 needed it because DEC-014 fixes five AI providers; this family has one, so the CHECK would be a vocabulary of one), and a COMPOSITE foreign key to the connection, because §3.3 requires a child to prove its parent is in the same Workspace and 060's row had no parent below the Workspace.

ONE DOCUMENT DISAGREES AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY CONTRADICTED. RFC-2026-012's inventory row reads "meta connections/accounts/bindings | health projection view only | BASE ROW CARRIES A CREDENTIAL REFERENCE (SECRET-4)". That parenthesis is the RFC's stated REASON, not its decision, and it is not true of this schema: app.meta_connections carries no credential_reference column and no foreign key into `private`, because 060 refused the same pointer in the same direction. **The DECISION that row states -- "health projection view only" -- is unaffected and is followed**, and §9.1's INTEGRATION-2 client projection ("health projection only") is an independent source for it. Owed to whoever maintains RFC-2026-012's inventory.

"private workspace" IS A ZONE AND A SCOPE, AND THE SCOPE IS AN OUTPUT RATHER THAN AN INPUT. §5's Scope column reads `workspace`, `global/workspace`, `workspace/business/page`, `user`, `business/page` and -- for audit.core -- `workspace/private`. The raw webhook inbox is the one row spelled "private workspace", and four documents say what it commits a batch to: §3.1 names "raw webhook" in the `private` row BY NAME with no direct grant; §14's gate checklist requires it not be exposed; §10's WEBHOOK-SHORT says "no tenant access"; and §11.1/5 keeps raw webhook out of the PDPA export an owner may request. §8.3 agrees in the matrix: "Raw token/webhook SELECT | N N N N N S".

DOES A CLIENT EVER READ A RAW WEBHOOK BODY? No. RFC-2026-021 keeps the client read allowlist EMPTY and RFC-2026-012's own inventory row for this family is the shortest in the document -- "raw webhook inbox | server-only | private, no direct grant". A raw provider payload is not the entry that opens that list, and this batch does not propose it as a candidate.

THE SCOPE COLUMN IS THEREFORE NULLABLE, which no other canonical scope column in this schema is, and the apply-time block refuses a later NOT NULL. A delivery arrives before anything knows whose it is: resolving it means matching the provider's account identifier against app.social_accounts, and that match can FAIL -- an unknown account, a replay, a forgery. NOT NULL would make exactly those deliveries unstorable, deleting the rows a security investigation wants most, and it would quietly reclassify the statement that reads them from DISCOVERED to CARRIED under RFC-2026-022 §3. The fixture loads one resolved and one unresolved delivery so the nullability is exercised rather than merely declared.

THE THREE VERBS OF "append/process/purge" HAVE NO ACTOR BETWEEN THEM, AND EACH ABSENCE HAS A DIFFERENT OWNER. §5 gives the raw webhook inbox the only three-verb mutability in the inventory and batch 110 grants no role any of them.

APPEND: no writer. §3.1 reaches `private` only "Server/worker ผ่าน typed service เท่านั้น", RFC-2026-012 §4 names what that is, and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that no command function exists. Owed to the batch that brings the command surface and to DATA-DEC-03.

PROCESS: no actor, and THIS HALF IS NOT WAITING FOR THE GUC. RFC-2026-022 §3's own table assigns "Raw token/webhook SELECT" to batches 110 and 131 and classifies it DISCOVERED, and §5/5 gives a discovered cell NO POLICY, PERMANENTLY, performed through a SECURITY DEFINER broker owned by a fifth not-a-path role (proposed name app_queue) that does not exist. Creating it belongs to the RFC that creates the worker. Batch 050 refused to build a writer for its outbox on the same ground -- "a correctly shaped table with no writer, and the writer is a decision with an owner rather than a column somebody forgot" -- and this batch names the owner. **A LATER READER MUST NOT "FIX" service-cannot-read-a-meta-webhook-delivery OR service-cannot-process-a-meta-webhook-delivery BY WRITING A POLICY**: they are permanent under §5/5, the cases say so in the `why` that prints in suite output, and the classification is recorded as data in db/foundation/lint/service-policy-map.json.

PURGE: no scheduler. §10's WEBHOOK-SHORT is a retention rule with a purge in it -- "30 วันหลัง processed; 90 วัน failure/DLQ ... redact/purge payload, retain dedupe hash longer" -- and batch 160 owns the retention job while §10's numbers need Product/Security/Legal approval before Paid Beta (§15). No window is encoded in a constraint, where it would read as ratified. What the batch provides is the columns each sweep would read -- processed_at for the 30-day window, failed_at for the 90-day one, redacted_at so a null body_ref after redaction is distinguishable from a delivery that never had a body -- with an index over each, and a body_ref that can be emptied while the dedupe hash §10 says to keep longer stays. Owed to batch 160 and to §10's own approval.

THE CHANNEL BINDING IS ASSIGNED TO NO BATCH BY THE REGISTRY, AND BOTH BATCHES THAT COULD OWN IT HAVE NOW DECLINED. §4's ERD gives CHANNEL_BINDING three parents -- BUSINESS_PROFILE, PAGE_CONTEXT_PROFILE and SOCIAL_ACCOUNT -- and §5 names "bindings" in TWO module rows, business.core and connector.meta, which §6's file ownership contract forbids ("one table has one owner"). §6's registry gives 110 "connection/account/webhook inbox" and gives 111 (A0 Integration) the "business-channel/social FK" -- the foreign key, not the table.

Batch 020 declined it in its own header ("either a dangling uuid column pointing at nothing or a foreign key this batch is forbidden to write ... Owed by 110/111") and batch 110 declines it for the same rule from the other side: migration invariant 6 puts a cross-module foreign key in an integration batch and the registry names 111 as its owner. THE CONSEQUENCE IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: §4's relation invariant 2 -- "Social Account ผูก Active Business เดียวในช่วงเวลาเดียวกัน" -- is a constraint ON the binding, and nothing in this schema enforces it, because the column pair it would be over does not exist. It is also why §12.6/2 and §8.6 cases 3 and 4 have no instance in this batch: the only row in this family that would carry a Business or a Page is the binding. **Owed to A0 and to whoever reconciles §5's two rows with §6's 111.** [2026-09-15, batch 111 (A0): DELIVERED the social key -- content_targets_social_scope_fk (workspace_id, social_account_id) -> app.social_accounts (workspace_id, id) -- and DECLINED the binding: three batches have now, and the business-channel half of §6's row stays owed to A0 with this entry as its record (C0-111 M2).]

§5 ASSIGNS connector.meta THE RETENTION CLASS `CONNECTION-HISTORY` AND §10 DEFINES NO SUCH CLASS. Its table has twenty-seven rows and none of them is that one. This is the THIRD family where §5 names a class §10 omits -- batch 030 reported it for `CATALOG` on industry.core and batch 050 for `LEDGER` on jobs.kernel -- and it is reported rather than resolved for the reason those two gave: §10's numbers need Product/Security/Legal approval and §15 forbids an agent choosing an open decision. A static test asserts the absence in the source document, so the day §10 gains the row the test fails and batch 160 has a number to use. The second inventory row's class, `WEBHOOK-SHORT`, IS defined, and everything this batch does about retention is done from it. **Owed to §10's own approval and to batch 160.**

§5 also calls the first row "mutable + HISTORY" and this batch creates no history table: `HISTORY` is defined as "immutable business/page/knowledge/content versions", §4's ERD gives META_CONNECTION and SOCIAL_ACCOUNT no version entity, and §6's registry gives 110 three things and no version table. Batch 021 refused to create workspace_member_scope_versions for the same reason -- "creating one would be reserving a table no registry row gives this batch". BATCH 160 PREP (2026-10-03; plan a0-batch-160-prep-plan-2026-10-03.md, db/foundation/lint/retention-map.json findings): the retention map carries meta_connections, social_accounts and private.meta_credential_references as finding rows under F160-01 -- no class, no row number, no behaviour -- and the absence above is OWED TO Q160-c (A1 Data, which amends ERD §5/§10 because docs/** is read-only here), then to Q160-a for the number. Not duplicated in open_blockers[192].

§9.3 ASKS FOR TWO THINGS ABOUT AN EXTERNAL ACCOUNT ID AND THIS BATCH STORES ONE. "External account ID: raw encrypted/private reference + stable hash for uniqueness". app.social_accounts.external_account_hash is the second half -- exactly 32 octets of sha256, unique per WORKSPACE for batch 050's reason about its consumer ledger (a conflicting insert on a global key is an oracle telling one tenant that another already holds that account). THE RAW IDENTIFIER IS NOT STORED ANYWHERE: the "encrypted" form needs a mechanism no decision in this repository names (§9.3's other encryption requirements are platform-level), and the "private reference" form needs the typed service §3.1 requires and RFC-2026-019 §2 measured as absent. Storing it plainly in `app` instead would be the one place this batch put a value §9.1 tells it to redact into the exposed schema. This is 010's treatment of an invitation token -- "store cryptographic hash only", §9.3's own first line -- applied one row over. **Owed to the batch that brings the typed service and to batch 120**, which is the first batch with a caller that has to address a Page at the provider. A static test asserts that no column named for a raw external identifier exists anywhere in the batch.

§8.3 GIVES THIS FAMILY THREE CLIENT-FACING ROWS AND BATCH 110 IMPLEMENTS NONE, WHICH IS A REFUSAL WITH A DIFFERENT REASON EACH TIME.

"Meta connection health SELECT | Y | Y | P | N | N | P" grants a HEALTH PROJECTION and not a row -- §9.1 gives INTEGRATION-2 the client projection "health projection only" with the storage rule "redact external identifiers", which is the shape batch 050 met in §8.4's "Job REDACTED STATUS SELECT". A projection is a security_invoker view (RFC-2026-012 §2) on an allowlist that is empty and grows only by RFC (RFC-2026-021). Against §4's criteria the candidate fails C1 and only C1: there is no `src/`, no client module and no screen in any source document that reads connection health. C7 does not apply -- these are TENANT tables. C2/C3 are the work, and this batch deliberately does not pre-empt them, because the projection's column list IS the substance of an entry and inventing the health columns here would be writing the entry's contents in the batch refusing to write the entry. **Owed to the RFC that opens the allowlist, in a new batch in this family's range.**

"Connect/disconnect/re-auth Meta | Y | P | N | N | N | P" is a COMMAND, and its essential half is outside the database. CONNECTING is an OAuth exchange with Meta and §3.4 forbids calling an external provider while holding a DB transaction, so a client INSERT could only ever write a connection row for a credential that does not exist. RE-AUTH is a rotation of a value in the vault. DISCONNECT looks implementable -- one timestamp -- and is the most misleading of the three: §11.4 step 2 spells the operation "Revoke browser sessions, push tokens, invitations, API/connector credentials", so the timestamp is the RECORD of a revocation and not the revocation, and a path that let a client stamp it without revoking anything would produce a row asserting something that did not happen. **Owed to RFC-2026-012 §4's command surface and to DATA-DEC-03.** The admin's `P` and the editor's `P` are additionally the capability set RFC-2026-020 §8 records as defined by no document.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR RFC-2026-021 §8.5: batch 110 grants `authenticated` NOTHING anywhere, so it adds no new row to the CLOSED list of inherited base-table grants that 030, 040 and 130 each grew while recording the debt. That is a consequence of the refusals above rather than a virtue of the batch, and the list still does not exist.

A DEAD DUPLICATE KEY IN AUTHORIZATION_CASE_COVERAGE WAS FOUND ON `main` AND REMOVED, AND IT IS THE DEFECT CLASS THE PARALLEL-INTEGRATION RECORD EXISTS TO PREDICT. tests/db/identity/isolation-cases.mjs declared key `10` TWICE. JavaScript keeps the last, so thirty-five lines were unreachable -- and they were the PRE-CORRECTION copies of batches 130's and 140's §8.6 case-9 paragraphs, still carrying "A FIFTH AND A SIXTH IMMUTABLE TABLE" and "THE FIFTH AND SIXTH IMMUTABLE TABLES": the exact ordinals the 2026-09-07 integration round corrected in the live copy of key 9. The correction landed and the false sentences survived beside it, in a key nothing reads.

evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/parallel-integration-2026-09-07.md §4 describes this shape exactly -- a seam that falls INSIDE an expression, parses, runs, and reports nothing -- and nothing in the repository could see it: a duplicate key is invisible to the parsed object and therefore to every assertion written about it. Nothing was lost by deleting it; every paragraph it held is present, corrected, in key 9. **What is new is the guard**: a test now reads the SOURCE of each coverage map and requires each key to be declared exactly once, which is a property the parsed object cannot be asked about.

A PINNED ORDINAL WENT FALSE AND WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN DELETED, WHICH IS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THE DEFECT §2 OF THE PARALLEL-INTEGRATION RECORD NAMES. Batch 060 wrote that `anonymous-cannot-read-a-credential-reference` was "the ONLY anonymous case in the suite whose declared object is `private` rather than `app`", in SMOKE_COVERAGE[6] and in the case's own `why`, and identity-isolation.test.mjs pinned the word with assert.match. Batch 110 adds two more such cases, so the sentence is false of the merged tree and the pin would have kept it alive. The note now states the SHAPE rather than a count, the test pins the shape, and both the note and the case record what the sentence said and why the branch that wrote it could not check it. A second claim in the same file -- "batch 060 creates the only table in `private` in the whole migration set" -- was the same shape and is replaced by what it was actually about: the widened lint is re-run over every migration up to 040 and must still find nothing.

BATCH 110 IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, for the STRUCTURAL reason 011, 020, 021, 030, 040, 041, 050 and 060 share rather than the executable-probe reason batch 140 gave. It creates four tables, two of them in `private`, and a fixture the instance has never received; and the declaration must name a TAIL of the ordered set, because a database holding 130 and 140 while missing 110 is DIVERGENT rather than behind and pendingDeclarationLint refuses a declaration that is not a tail. 110 sorts between 060 and 130, so the tail stays contiguous at eleven batches. THE MIGRATION SET IS NOW THIRTEEN FILES. CI applies all of them to a postgres:17 container on every pull request; this DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so every live claim in batch 110 -- the apply-time block, the 370 isolation cases and the two new negative-control entries -- is proven by a CI round and by nothing else. What remains unverified even then is everything needing the PROVISIONED instance rather than a container: the CI shim's roles are ones we created, so a green round means "the policies still do what they did", never "this works on Supabase".

BATCH 060 CREATED NO REQUEST LOG AND BATCH 061 IS THE SECOND BATCH TO REACH THE SAME REGISTRY GAP, which is what turns one batch's reading into evidence. 061 was dispatched with the premise that 060 had created an AI request log and that a usage event meters a row in it. It had not: 060_ai_gateway.sql creates the model registry, the workspace's model policy and the credential reference, and says in terms that "GENERATION RUNS ARE NOT CREATED HERE ... no batch in the whole 000-180 registry is given a generation-run table, and 061 ... is 'quota/reservation/usage ledger', which is metering rather than run history". §5's inventory row for `ai.gateway` names generation runs and §6's registry gives them to nobody.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR 061, STATED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED A THIRD TIME: there is no row for app.usage_events to reference and no second definition of a unit of consumption to reconcile against. A unit of consumption is defined in exactly one place -- CTR-USG-001's six `dimension` values crossed with its five `quantity.unit` values, both from OB-004 -- and nothing in 060 defines one at all. The one vocabulary the two batches both carry is `provider`, and they are DIFFERENT SETS by their own sources' definitions: 060 pins DEC-014's five AI providers, CTR-USG-001 types `attribution.provider_key` as a pattern with no enumeration, and four of its six dimensions (storage, egress, media processing, publish) are not served by an AI provider at all -- so narrowing 061's column into 060's CHECK would make four of six dimensions unrecordable. 061 writes no foreign key into app.ai_models for the same reason: an object-storage egress charge would have to hold a row in the AI model registry. **Owed to A0 and to whichever batch §6 is amended to name.**

THE LEDGER/AGGREGATE QUESTION §5 ASKS AND DOES NOT ANSWER, ANSWERED IN 061 AND RECORDED HERE BECAUSE BATCH 132 INHERITS IT. §5 gives metering.core the mutability "append-only ledger + aggregate" -- two shapes -- and a ledger that may only be inserted and an aggregate that must move as the ledger grows cannot both be immutable. 061's four answers, each from a document:

(1) THE LEDGER CARRIES THE TRUTH. §3.2 ("Immutable version/evidence/decision/USAGE/audit history"), §4 invariant 8 ("Approval/Usage/Audit history เป็น immutable") and §8.4 ("Usage ledger INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE | N N N N N S/N" -- the `S` is the INSERT and UPDATE/DELETE is `N` for every role INCLUDING the service) all say the same thing. app.usage_events therefore holds no UPDATE or DELETE grant and no UPDATE or DELETE policy for any role, has no updated_at and no trigger, and the migration asserts both halves against the live ACL and the live policy catalog at apply time.

(2) THE QUOTA BUCKET IS DERIVED and therefore mutable: an aggregate is a statement ABOUT history rather than history, which is why §3.2 and §4/8 name the second and not the first.

(3) NOBODY MAY MOVE IT TODAY. §8's four matrices contain exactly two metering rows -- the summary SELECT and the ledger INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE -- and NEITHER is about writing a quota bucket, so the cell is denied by default (030's reading of the same silence). app_worker holds a COLUMN-SCOPED UPDATE on the three derived columns plus updated_at and NO POLICY, so FORCE row level security refuses it and the refusal is attributable to RLS rather than to a forgotten grant; the columns that say WHICH bucket a row is -- id, both scope columns, dimension, quantity_unit, period_start, period_end -- are outside that grant, so §8.5's "ห้ามย้าย row ข้าม tenant ด้วย update" holds by a COLUMN LIST rather than by an absent verb, which is the distinction independent review had to correct on 060. **The writer is batch 132 ("entitlement-metering resolver", A0 Integration + A6, depending on 061 and 130), and the identity that would run it does not exist either (RFC-2026-022 §5/8).**

(4) WHEN THEY DISAGREE THE LEDGER WINS, BY CONSTRUCTION, AND 061 WRITES NO RECONCILIATION -- no trigger on the ledger, no view, no function. A mechanism keeping the two equal would have to decide which events fall in which bucket when one arrives after its period closed, whether a `provider_reported` event subtracts the `estimated` one it supersedes, whether an expired hold is released by the sweep or by the next recompute, and whether the bucket is authoritative between recomputes. CTR-USG-001's freeze boundary puts OB-008's reconciliation algorithm outside itself, §6 gives the resolver to 132, and §15 forbids an agent closing an open decision. WHAT IS BUILT INSTEAD MAKES THE DISAGREEMENT DETECTABLE RATHER THAN RESOLVABLE: `computed_through` is a watermark recording what the derived row claims to cover, so "this bucket is wrong" is a query over the ledger anyone can run, and a bucket whose watermark is NULL claims nothing rather than claiming zero. A derived value that cannot be checked against its source is the unfalsifiable shape this repository keeps removing. **Owed to batch 132 and to OB-008.**

BATCH 061's LEDGER COLUMNS COME FROM CTR-USG-001, WHICH IS `Draft` AND WHOSE OWNER IS THIS BATCH'S OWN OWNER PAIR (A0+A6), AND FOUR DIVERGENCES ARE DECLARED RATHER THAN QUIET. That is 140's situation with CTR-AUD-001 repeated, and CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md's conflict order is why the contract decides: the Contract Catalog sits at position 2 and this repository's data package at 4.

(a) `usage_id` is a `uuid` and is NOT the primary key. No client role holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on app.audit_logs or app.security_events, so a member can neither forge a record about themselves nor edit nor remove one, and the refusal is 42501 before row level security is consulted. AGAINST `app_worker`: guaranteed for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. **AGAINST A ROLE THAT BYPASSES ROW LEVEL SECURITY: NOT GUARANTEED, AND FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY BUYS NOTHING.** `postgres` owns every table in `app` and holds BYPASSRLS (RFC-2026-021 §2/M2, and scripts/db/run.mjs's KNOWN_BYPASS pins the set), and BYPASSRLS beats FORCE -- forcing makes the OWNER subject to policies, and a bypassing role is outside the row-security system whether or not it owns the table. The owner can also disable RLS, drop a policy, grant itself a verb, delete, truncate and drop the table.

WHAT IS DONE ABOUT IT, AND WHAT IS NOT. §8.5's rule for an immutable table is "no user update/delete policy AND a command/trigger/privilege defense as appropriate"; batches 020, 030 and 040 took the privilege half, and 140 is the first table where the trigger half is appropriate, because it is the first whose adversary can hold the privilege. private.refuse_mutation() raises SQLSTATE ZZ140 on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE for every role including the owner, and 140_audit.sql PROVES it by execution at apply time rather than citing it (RFC-2026-020 §6.2's rule): it writes a probe row as the migration role -- which owns the table and bypasses RLS -- requires all three verbs to raise, and rolls the probe back. **ITS LIMIT: the owner can `alter table ... disable trigger all` and then delete whatever it likes.** This is tamper RESISTANCE, not tamper EVIDENCE. It raises the cost from one statement to two and makes the first an act nobody performs by accident; a determined owner is not stopped and nothing in a database can stop one. Tamper evidence against that adversary is a hash chain, an append-only store outside this database, or WORM storage -- and CTR-AUD-001's freeze boundary lists "the audit STORE, its append-only or immutability mechanism, and any tamper evidence" as OPEN, with its untestable_by_schema note saying there is no hash chain field "because no source specifies one". This batch does not invent one. **Owed to A1 Security and to whoever freezes CTR-AUD-001.** Q141-c ANSWERED 2026-10-04 by the Owner's `เิาตามแนะนำ` (2026-10-04, product-owner-disposition-2026-10-03-batch-150.md), as A0 recommended: tamper RESISTANCE (the refusal trigger and the absent grants) is enough until G1, and the missing tamper EVIDENCE (a hash chain or an external append-only store) is an ACCEPTED RISK until then. NO CLIENT ROLE READS AUDIT OR SECURITY EVENTS AT ALL, WHICH REFUSES FIVE §8.4 CELLS AND IS THE batch's largest deliberate omission. §8.4 gives "Tenant audit SELECT" Y to the owner, P to the admin, O to the editor, "approval trail" to the approver and N to the viewer, and "Security event details" P to the owner. Batch 140 implements none: RFC-2026-012 decision 2 puts a client read behind a named security_invoker view -- and its inventory classifies these two families "safe view only" and "server-only, owner P only", the only two rows in it carrying a redaction qualifier -- while RFC-2026-021 §7/3 keeps that allowlist EMPTY, §4's C1 (a named CLIENT caller exists) fails exactly as it failed for the industry catalog, and §8.5 says the list of inherited base-table grants "is CLOSED: any new one fails". §9.1's projection rules for AUTH-3 and SECURITY-4 are "minimum role projection" and "security/admin safe view only", and a base-table grant projects nothing.

TWO OF THE FIVE CELLS WOULD HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTABLE AND ARE NAMED, so this is a refusal rather than an oversight: the owner's `Y` is `app.workspace_member_role(workspace_id) = 'owner'`, and the editor's `O` is `actor_kind = 'user' and actor_id = (select auth.uid())::text` -- the one cell in the matrix where the reader IS the subject of the record. THE OTHER THREE CANNOT BE: the admin's `P` needs the capability set no document defines (RFC-2026-020 §8), and the approver's cell is literally "approval trail", a subset scoped by approval tables that are batch 090 and do not exist. Five isolation cases assert the present refusal, one per cell, at the GRANT layer, so the day an allowlist entry opens one, exactly one line changes. **Owed to the RFC that opens the allowlist, in a new batch in this family's range, with the safe view §9.1 asks for.** §11.1's "Tenant-visible audit trail" is NOT blocked by this: export is a background job (batch 160), not a client read.

TWO PLACES WHERE THE BASELINE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT AUDIT, FOUND BY IMPLEMENTING IT AND RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY A BATCH. (1) §8.4 marks "Audit/security UPDATE/DELETE" `N` for every role INCLUDING the service, and §10 gives the AUDIT class "anonymize actor where allowed; purge after policy" and the SECURITY class "hash/anonymize PII; retain active investigation/legal hold" -- every one of which is an UPDATE or a DELETE that §8.4 grants nobody. Batch 140 obeys §8.4: no role holds either verb, and private.refuse_mutation() refuses them for `app_maintenance` as well. So THE RETENTION JOB CANNOT RUN, and batch 160 cannot fix it with a grant -- it must replace that trigger function in a forward migration a reviewer reads, or narrow it to a named path. That is deliberate: a trigger with a hole for a role that holds no grant and no policy yet would be a permission nobody reviewed against a caller. **Owed to §10's own approval, to DATA-DEC-06 and to batch 160.** (2) §5 scopes audit.core "workspace/private" and app.security_events is the private half. It is created in `app` instead, because §3.1 reaches `private` only "through a typed service" and none exists (RFC-2026-019 §2), while scripts/db/run.mjs's catalog lint FAILS the build when any service role holds USAGE on private. A table in `private` today is reachable by NO ROLE, so no isolation case could distinguish an RLS refusal from a missing grant from a missing schema privilege, and its isolation would be unprovable -- the unfalsifiable shape RFC-2026-016 §4 retired "force where compatible" for being. **Owed to the batch that brings the typed service (RFC-2026-012 §4, DATA-DEC-03).**

NEITHER AUDIT TABLE CARRIES A FOREIGN KEY, SO §4 INVARIANT 10 IS NOT ENFORCED FOR THIS FAMILY. Every other tenant table in this schema references its parent over the whole scope path, and §3.3 asks for it. app.audit_logs and app.security_events reference nothing -- not app.workspaces, not app.business_profiles, not app.page_context_profiles -- because §11.4's REQUIRED ORDER purges tenant content in step 7 and "anonymize/RETAIN finance, audit, security minimum required records" in step 8. An audit record must outlive the rows it names, and a foreign key makes that impossible in both directions at once: either the audit row blocks a PDPA deletion the same document orders, or the purge deletes a record this table refuses to delete. §11.2 says the same thing about actors ("Content/approval/audit history ห้าม cascade delete") and every batch since 010 has applied it to created_by; 140 applies it to the SCOPE columns, which is new.

THE COST: an audit row naming a Business that belongs to a different Workspace is refused by nothing in this schema and cannot be. What refuses it is the producer -- CTR-AUD-001 embeds CTR-TEN-001, whose trust boundary reads "Server-resolved only after membership and Workspace→Business→Page relation validation; client-supplied context is untrusted input" -- and batch 141 is where a producer able to violate it will exist. It is also why this batch writes no `rejected` isolation case: there is no constraint for one to be about, and a case demanding an outcome a correct database cannot produce would be the suite claiming a control nobody built. **Owed to batch 141 and to CTR-AUD-001's freeze.** BATCH 141 (migration 172): the producer exists and copies its scope from the changed row (RFC-2026-026 §3.6): a workspace carries no business or page, so the closing command's rows name none, a refusal row names none by the policy (§3.3/4), and the copy is held statically (foundation-contract, the closing command's body) and by rls-smoke's read-back. The POLICY-side relation check stays owed here, with the missing foreign key (Q-026-2), for the first command whose rows name a business.

BATCH 140's COLUMNS COME FROM A DRAFT CONTRACT, WHICH IS A DEPARTURE FROM EVERY BATCH BEFORE IT AND IS DECLARED RATHER THAN QUIET. §5 classifies audit.core and NAMES NO COLUMN, and 020, 030 and 040 each recorded that they therefore invented nothing. 140 does not have to: contract-catalog/shared-kernel/ctr-aud-001/ fixes the audit record's fields by name with a source citation on each, and CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md's conflict order puts the Contract Catalog at position 2 where the Core Database/RLS document sits at 4. **CTR-AUD-001's status is `Draft`, its owner is A0+A6, and its freeze_boundary lists the audit STORE as open -- which is this batch.** So the columns are read from a contract that may still move, and four divergences are declared in the migration header: no `details` column at all (the contract declares the bag and holds it empty at maxProperties 0, and §5 forbids an untyped document column); no `locale` and no `timezone` (both `const` in CTR-TEN-001, so a column would store one value forever); `error` as ONE column rather than CTR-ERR-001's six; and tenant_context flattened into §3.3's canonical names rather than stored as a document. Two of the contract's `allOf` rules -- which its own untestable_by_schema note calls cross-field consistency JSON Schema in this subset cannot express -- are written as named CHECK constraints, so the STORE enforces what the schema could only fail at the edge. **A0 and A6 own CTR-AUD-001 and should countersign this reading before its freeze; if the contract moves, the forward fix is a new batch in this family's range, never an edit to 140.** **BATCH 141 PREP READ 140 AGAINST CTR-AUD-001 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (2026-10-03, plan a0-batch-141-prep-plan-2026-10-03.md; test-kits/db/fixtures/ctr-aud-001/store-conformance.json) AND FOUND FOUR MORE DIVERGENCES THAT 140 DOES NOT DECLARE.** They are pinned as a closed list, so the day the contract or the store moves the test fails by name, and they are OWED TO Q141-b (A0+A6) -- recorded, NOT decided, and not a reason to edit 140: (F1) the contract's `audit_id` (a string, minLength 1) is stored as `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` -- a rename and a narrowing, so no contract example (`aud_synthetic_0001` ...) is storable; (F2) CTR-TEN-001's workspace_id, business_profile_id and page_context_profile_id are strings and the store's are uuid -- 140 declares the flattening, not the narrowing; (F3) actor, correlation_id and causation_id appear twice in the contract (root and tenant_context) and correlation_id a third time in error, with nothing checking the copies agree (the manifest's untestable_by_schema note 3 names the correlation_id copy; the same holds, unstated, for actor and causation_id), while the store has one column each, so a contract-valid record whose copies differ cannot be stored and no source says which copy a producer writes; (F4) `created_at` has no contract property and is explained in a column comment, not declared. Q141-b ANSWERED 2026-10-04 by the Owner's `เิาตามแนะนำ` (2026-10-04, product-owner-disposition-2026-10-03-batch-150.md), as A0 recommended: CTR-AUD-001 is to be countersigned as batch 140 reads it, which countersigns F1-F4 of the batch 141 prep by name (product-owner-disposition-2026-10-03-batch-141-prep.md §5). BATCH 140 IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, and for a reason that is NOT the structural one 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040 share. Each of those depends on an object an earlier undeployed batch creates. 140 depends on none: no foreign key, no helper call, no policy, so it would apply to the instance exactly as it stands. It is declared because the declaration must name a TAIL of the ordered set -- a database missing a middle batch while holding later ones is DIVERGENT rather than behind -- and, more to the point, because 140's apply-time block WRITES A PROBE ROW into app.audit_logs as the migration role, attempts an UPDATE, a DELETE and a TRUNCATE against it and rolls the whole probe back. Doing that to a live database in order to make a lint pass is the inversion 011's header refuses, one table further along and on an audit log. THE MIGRATION SET IS NOW TWELVE FILES -- 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010, 011, 020, 021, 030, 040 and 140, counted from the tree. CI applies all twelve to a postgres:17 container on every pull request; this DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so every live claim in batch 140 -- the apply-time block including its executable trigger proof, 235 isolation cases and nine negative-control entries -- is proven by a CI round and by nothing else. THAT ROUND IS NOW GREEN: run 34048645398, 9m24s, with `applied 140_audit.sql` (the apply-time block, including its executable trigger probe, ran and passed), `db-rls-smoke: 235 isolation case(s) passed`, and both new negative-control entries noticing exactly the two cases each was declared to rest on. **What is still unverified is everything that needs the PROVISIONED instance rather than a container**: the CI shim's roles are ones we created, so a green round means "the policies still do what they did", never "this works on Supabase".

CI FOUND A CASE THAT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN FOUND WITHOUT A DATABASE, and the shape is worth keeping rather than only the fix. `__SELF__` in an isolation case means "the subject of the identity running this case", and TWO of the four identity helpers have none: `as_anonymous` and `as_service` set a role and a claim set with no `sub`. Batch 040's `service-cannot-create-a-knowledge-item` used `__SELF__` for created_by, the substitution returned `undefined`, the driver inlined it as the literal text 'undefined', and Postgres answered 22P02 -- "invalid input syntax for type uuid" -- which `expectDenied` CORRECTLY refused as not an RLS refusal. One case in 209; the other 208 passed and all eleven migrations applied.

Nothing static could have seen it: `__SELF__` is a string and a missing subject is a runtime `undefined`. It is a BUILD ERROR now -- `resolvePlaceholders` raises rather than substituting -- and a test exercises the function itself rather than a restatement of it, in both directions: the throw for a subjectless helper, and a real substitution for one that has a subject, so the guard cannot be made to pass by making it inert. The case names the workspace owner's subject and says why the value is arbitrary: app_worker holds NO POLICY on the table, so there is no WITH CHECK to compare a subject against and the refusal cannot be about that column.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE HARNESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE CASE: the static suite proves the instrument is honest and the live suite proves the policies. A defect in how a case ADDRESSES the database falls between them, and the only reason this one was cheap is that `expectDenied` refuses an outcome it cannot classify instead of treating any error as a denial. The guard held; the case was wrong.

RFC-2026-021 WAS APPROVED WHILE BATCH 040 WAS BEING WRITTEN, and it settles one thing 040 had been treating as inherited convention while creating a debt 040 makes larger. §7/4 decides that `anon` is granted NOTHING anywhere our migrations reach -- no schema USAGE, no table or column privilege, no function EXECUTE -- and gives the structural reason a batch could not give for itself: the first anon grant is `grant usage on schema app`, which changes the DENIAL LAYER of every object in app at once. Batch 040 grants anon nothing, both of its anonymous cases declare the refusal on the SCHEMA, and a static test now holds every anonymous knowledge case to that object so widening it fails rather than passing more quietly.

THE DEBT: §8.5 names the inherited `authenticated` base-table grants in 010, 020 and 021 and says the known-exceptions list enumerating them must be CLOSED -- "any new one fails" -- while §10 says those grants are not what the RFC decides and owes them to batch 170. That list does not exist yet. Batch 030 wrote new grants of the same shape on app.industry_assignments and batch 040 writes new ones on two knowledge tables, both AFTER the list was described and BEFORE it exists, so whoever writes it will enumerate FIVE batches rather than three. That is recorded here and in 040's own header rather than absorbed. It is a debt rather than a contradiction for the reason 030's header drew and RFC-2026-021's Status line confirms: every grant in 040 is COLUMN-SCOPED and bounded by a predicate row level security can express (`app.is_active_member(workspace_id)`), so a drift reaches one workspace and the suite proves the boundary -- "a column-scoped grant is not a table grant, so column drift is loud in the shape batch 010 writes". The RFC's reasoning is load-bearing about a GLOBAL table, which 040 does not create.

BATCH 040 IS DECLARED NOT APPLIED TO THE PROVISIONED INSTANCE, extending the tail 011, 020, 021 and 030 already form. Its knowledge policies call app.is_active_member and app.workspace_member_role (011), its narrowing calls app.member_scope_admits_business and app.member_scope_admits_page (021), and app.knowledge_items carries composite foreign keys into BOTH tables 020 creates. A batch cannot be applied to a database missing the batch it is built on. THE MIGRATION SET IS NOW ELEVEN FILES -- 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010, 011, 020, 021, 030 and 040, counted from the tree rather than carried forward, because an earlier entry in this list read "NINE" for two batches after it stopped being true. CI applies all eleven to a postgres:17 container on every pull request; this DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so every live claim in batch 040 -- both apply-time blocks, 209 isolation cases, the authz proofs and seven negative-control entries -- is proven by a CI round and by nothing else.

A KNOWLEDGE VERSION CAN BE WRITTEN WHOSE CONTENT NEVER WAS THE ITEM'S CONTENT, and RLS cannot fix it. Batch 040 grants a client INSERT on app.knowledge_item_versions and INSERT/UPDATE on app.knowledge_items, and no command function exists for knowledge.core -- the data package specifies none -- so a client writes the item and its version in two statements with nothing binding them into one transaction. Batch 020 recorded the same gap about business versions; it is LARGER here because the content is CONTENT-2 rather than a display name. It is owed to the command surface, not to a policy, and 040 refused to invent a trigger for it (§15). The narrowing does close the adjacent hole: a version can only be written for an item the caller can reach.

A PAGE-SCOPED EDITOR MAY WRITE BUSINESS-LEVEL KNOWLEDGE, which reaches every Page under that Business. This follows from batch 021's `app.member_scope_covers_business` counting a `page` scope row on its PARENT Business -- chosen there so a member scoped to one Page can still read the Business their Page hangs from -- and batch 030 met the same consequence on the industry assignment and gave the same answer: it is 021's definition and not a later batch's to change. Batch 040 CONSUMES it and asserts the behaviour POSITIVELY (`page-editor-a-can-update-the-business-level-knowledge-item-of-business-a1`), so the day somebody decides it is wrong a test moves in a diff instead of a boundary moving in silence. If it is wrong it is wrong in 021, and correcting it is a decision about the helper.

THREE CONTROLS WERE FOUND TOO WEAK WHILE BATCH 040 WAS WRITTEN, all in DB-00's own files, and all three are fixed here rather than reported. (1) db/foundation/test-helpers/rls-assertions.mjs attributed a refusal to an object with the pattern `policy[^"]*for table`, which cannot cross the quotes around a policy NAME -- and Postgres includes the name only when a RESTRICTIVE policy is what refused. So EVERY restrictive refusal attributed to no object, and the only way to assert one was to declare no layer at all, which is the unattributed shape C0's review D6 removed. Batches 021 and 030 added restrictive policies but no case where the permissive check PASSES and the restrictive one refuses; 040's scoped-editor writes are the first. (2) scripts/db/rls-smoke.mjs printed its §12.6 coverage report filtered on `!covered`, so a truthy PARTIAL label vanished -- §12.6/8 has read `negative-half` since batch 010 and had never once appeared in that report. (3) The rule requiring every table the CI negative control names to be created by a migration read four filenames written by hand, so a batch adding a table AND its entry failed it; it reads the directory now.

BATCH 040's OWN PROBE ROUND FOUND TWO OF ITS ASSERTIONS TOO WEAK BEFORE IT LANDED, and the record says so rather than reporting a clean sweep (evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a2-batch-040-probes-2026-09-06.md). A policy's USING and its WITH CHECK are two predicates in two catalog columns; both the static test and the migration's apply-time block were matching the WHOLE policy body, so gutting one half while leaving the other intact was NOT NOTICED. That state is worse than it sounds: a restrictive narrowing whose USING has been gutted filters nothing on READ for the member it exists to narrow while still refusing that member's writes -- the leak, without the symptom. Both were closed before the second round. THE GENERAL SHAPE IS NOT CLOSED: nothing stops a future assertion about a policy from matching the whole body when the property belongs to one half, and a rule that could enforce it would need to know which properties are per-clause.

§8.2 GIVES THE SERVICE `P` ON KNOWLEDGE AND NO DOCUMENT DEFINES IT, so batch 040 writes app_worker grants and no policy, exactly as 010, 020, 021 and 030 do. §12.6/8's positive half stays unasserted for the reason it has stayed unasserted since batch 010: asserting it would require inventing the permission first. What 040 adds is more negative evidence -- the service reads zero rows from both tables while holding grants on both, its item UPDATE is FILTERED and witnessed, and its version UPDATE and DELETE are refused at the GRANT layer.

The live half runs in CI and nowhere else. A Postgres service container gives db-migrate-clean, db-schema-lint and db-rls-smoke a real database on every pull request; all NINE migration batches apply -- 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010, 011, 020 and 021, counted from the tree rather than carried forward -- and the schema lint passes. The count read "five" from the moment batch 004 was added two commits later in the same night, on the same package, in a commit whose own blocker text says "Batch 004 exists"; C0's review D10 found it. This DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so the targets refuse locally and every live change is proven by a CI round, not from a shell. db-migrate-upgrade and db-seed-replay remain unproven for a different reason: neither has a fixture to run against, and both say so rather than reporting a pass.

STALE STATUS, KEPT AS A RECORD: RFC-2026-021 was APPROVED on 2026-09-06 (its status line). MEASURED CORRECTION TO AN APPROVED DECISION'S REASONING. RFC-2026-012 §2 forbids base-table client reads because 'column drift is silent'. The negative control's reported count now counts FAILED CASE LINES rather than every indented line containing a parenthesis, which had been sweeping the coverage report and the authz-proof lines in with them. The control itself was never wrong: it greps case ids, and it bit correctly on every family. Only the sentence describing what it had done was wrong -- which is the kind of defect that survives longest, because nothing it guards ever fails.

The CI negative control runs PER TABLE FAMILY as of 2026-09-06, and each entry requires a failed case whose id matches that table's own pattern. BATCH 030 ADDS THE FIFTH, SIXTH AND SEVENTH ENTRIES -- one for each table it creates -- and one of them is a shape this control has not had before. app.industry_assignments is an ordinary tenant entry: disabling row level security there lets tenant A read tenant B's assignment, lets a member scoped to one Business read another's, and lets the suspended member and the service identity read rows they must not see; four cases match its pattern.

app.industry_packs AND app.industry_pack_versions ARE THE NEW SHAPE, and the reason is recorded in the workflow beside the entries rather than only here. They belong to NO WORKSPACE, so there is no tenant boundary for the control to dissolve, and batch 030 grants no client role any privilege on them at all (RFC-2026-012 §2/3: the read allowlist starts empty and grows only by RFC). Every client case against them is a PRIVILEGE-layer refusal, and disabling row level security does not restore a grant nobody made -- so none of those cases would notice. The entries bite through the ONE grant that exists: app_worker holds SELECT and no policy, which is batch 010's shape for making a service denial attributable to RLS rather than to a forgotten GRANT, so with RLS off the service reads the catalog and `service-sees-zero-*` fails. EACH OF THOSE TWO ENTRIES THEREFORE RESTS ON EXACTLY ONE CASE. That is a weaker control than the others and it is named as one: tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs asserts each of those cases by id, by outcome kind and by identity helper, so deleting the case fails the build instead of leaving an entry that disables something nothing notices. RFC-2026-020 is APPROVED (2026-09-06) and batch 011 lands it: db/foundation/migrations/011_authorization_helpers.sql creates app_authz, its single narrow SELECT policy on app.workspace_members, three SECURITY DEFINER helpers it owns, and the roster policy implementing §8.1's "Member list SELECT: Owner Y, Admin Y". THE CONTROL IS THE PART TO REVIEW. The obvious control -- copy the helper, flip to SECURITY INVOKER, show that one inlines -- passes while proving NOTHING, for two independent reasons either of which alone is fatal: PostgreSQL will not inline a SQL function carrying a SET clause (the helper has `set search_path = ''`), and will not inline one with a FROM clause in any security mode (the helper reads a table). Both sides would have read "not inlined" and the discriminator would never have discriminated. The pair therefore differs in prosecdef and nothing else -- same body, no SET clause, no FROM -- using the shape RFC-2026-020 §2.4 already measured being inlined on the instance. Measured: the INVOKER half's plan contains its body (`Output: (((NULLIF(current_setting(...))::jsonb ->> 'sub'::text))::uuid`), the DEFINER half's contains a call. If the definer half ever inlines, the proof reports the decision WRONG and the batch must be reverted rather than worked around; that branch is executed locally against a fake runner.

D2 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — REPAIRED. WAS: the exemption register declared a granularity of role x table x operation and the lint enforced none of it. Rows were matched to a table by NAME alone, so a row scoped as narrowly as the shape allows -- {role: 'app_worker', operation: 'select'} -- bought its table a blanket pass, and the same row suppressed rls_enabled as well as rls_forced, which let one register row excuse a tenant table having no row level security at all.

IS NOW: the lint enforces what the catalog can CORROBORATE, and scripts/db/run.mjs and the register's own _what_the_catalog_can_corroborate say plainly what that is. relforcerowsecurity is a TABLE property -- one value for every role and every operation at once -- so it corroborates exactly one row, role '*' with operation 'all', and only such a row suppresses the unforced-table finding. rolbypassrls and rolsuper are ROLE properties holding for every table at once, so a row naming a role is checked against that role's own attributes and suppresses no table finding; naming a table in it narrows nothing. IS NOW: db/foundation/test-helpers/rls-assertions.mjs carries denialObject() beside denialLayer(), reading which relation, schema or function the message names, and expectDeniedBy takes the case's declared { kind, name }. The KIND is declared rather than inferred, and writing the four declarations is where this stopped being bookkeeping. Two of the cases are `authenticated`, which holds USAGE on schema app (010:390), so a read it may not make is refused on the TABLE: { table, workspace_invitations } for both. THE SECRET-4 CONTROL ON private.push_subscription_references IS A COLUMN ALLOWLIST AND NOT A SCANNER, AND THE REASON GENERALISES. §9.1 lists "push token" as one of its four examples of SECRET-4 and gives that class "vault/encrypted secret store; never plaintext DB/log". A Web Push subscription is an ENDPOINT — a bearer capability URL — plus the p256dh and auth KEYS. The repository's secret scan runs over this batch's migration and fixture on every `npm run check` and COULD NOT CATCH ANY OF THE THREE: an endpoint is an ordinary https URL at a vendor host, indistinguishable in shape from a link, and the two keys are base64url with no vendor prefix. So the control cannot be "we will notice a secret if one appears"; it has to be that the secret HAS NO COLUMN TO APPEAR IN, which is what the apply-time allowlist enforces — a later batch adding `endpoint text` fails the migration rather than the code review. RECORDED FOR THE BATCHES AFTER THIS ONE: 110 (raw Meta webhook inbox, PROVIDER-3/SECRET-4) and 131 (payment webhook) face the same shape, and a denylist of column names somebody thought of is defeated by the one they did not.

THE FINDING FOR THE PROGRAM RATHER THAN FOR THIS BATCH: reversal probes cannot catch an ordinal. A probe reverses an assertion and asks whether something notices; an ordinal is a sentence that is TRUE OF THE BRANCH AND FALSE OF THE TREE, and the tree does not exist while the branch is being written. Nothing in this repository can check one, which is exactly why the 2026-09-07 integration concluded that a batch must not write one at all. What a build CAN hold is the family member the new rule `neither coverage map declares a key twice` catches — and the duplicate key that rule found had been carrying two of the ordinals that integration corrected everywhere a program could see.

BATCH 131 STORES §9.3's STABLE HASH AND REFUSES THE RAW PROVIDER REFERENCE, WHICH LEAVES §13.1's RECONCILIATION UNDETECTABLE. §9.3 asks for a "raw encrypted/private reference + stable hash for uniqueness" and this batch stores only the second: `provider_event_hash`, `provider_invoice_hash` and `provider_payment_hash` are sha256 digests with a 32-byte floor, and no `evt_`, `in_` or `pi_` value exists anywhere in the schema. So app.billing_webhook_receipts is a correctly shaped inbox with no reader and no writer, which is 050's state on the outbox one family over. app.billing_invoices.provider_revision IS THE ORDERING §8.4 REQUIRES AND NOTHING ENFORCES ITS MONOTONICITY. §8.4: "Event type ไม่ใช่คำสั่งให้ set state แบบ blind", "ก่อนลดสิทธิ์หรือกรณี event เก่ากว่า projection ให้ fetch Subscription/Invoice ล่าสุดจาก Stripe", and "เก็บ provider_created_at, processed_at, provider object ID และ projection revision". BATCH 131 ADDS A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT TO A MERGED TABLE AS A FORWARD FIX, AND THE ROLLOUT CLAUSE INVARIANT 3 REQUIRES IS PAID ONLY FOR AN EMPTY TABLE. `alter table app.billing_subscriptions add constraint billing_subscriptions_workspace_key unique (workspace_id, id)` is needed because §3.3 requires a child of a tenant parent to take a composite foreign key, §4 invariant 10 states the failure it prevents, and batch 130's PARTIAL unique index cannot be a foreign key target. THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: `ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and builds an index, which is instantaneous only because app.billing_subscriptions is empty on every instance this batch can reach. On a populated instance the non-blocking path is invariant 4's -- `create unique index concurrently` outside a transaction, then `add constraint ... using index` -- which scripts/db/run.mjs does not support. Owed to A0 as the owner of the runner, before any batch alters a populated table.

§8.3's INBOX STATE MACHINE HAS FIVE STATES AND app.billing_webhook_receipts STORES NO STATUS COLUMN, WHICH IS THIS BATCH'S ONE DEPARTURE FROM A DIAGRAM A DOCUMENT ACTUALLY CONTAINS. RECEIVED, PROCESSED, RETRYABLE and DEAD_LETTER are the presence or absence of `processed_at`, `dead_lettered_at` and `next_attempt_at`; the fifth, PROCESSING, is distinguishable from RECEIVED only by a LEASE, which is `app.jobs`' lease_owner/lease_expires_at pair and which batch 050 owns. That is the same gap the queue has and it is the same owner's: owed to the lease mechanism batch 050 owns and to whoever freezes CTR-JOB-001's lifecycle.

BATCH 132 HAS NO §5 INVENTORY ROW, AND EVERY PROPERTY A TABLE WOULD NEED COMES FROM ONE. §5's Canonical Data Dictionary Summary has a row for `metering.core` and a row for `billing.core` and no third row for a resolver. THE JOIN AN EFFECTIVE LIMIT RESOLVER IS FOR DOES NOT EXIST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. BATCH 132 NEEDS ALL FOUR OF THE QUESTIONS BATCH 061 RECORDED AS UNDECIDED, AND AVOIDS NONE. 061 lists what a mechanism keeping the ledger and the bucket equal would have to decide and says a trigger there "would be this batch writing 132, in the quietest place available". Applied to a resolver: (1) WHICH EVENTS FALL IN WHICH BUCKET WHEN AN EVENT ARRIVES AFTER ITS PERIOD CLOSED decides the denominator of every answer, and the schema already holds two candidate timestamps pointing different ways -- `occurred_at`, which `usage_events_bucket_recompute_idx` is keyed on, and `computed_through`, a watermark over rows CREATED at or before an instant. (3) WHETHER AN EXPIRED RESERVATION IS RELEASED BY THE SWEEP OR BY THE NEXT RECOMPUTE decides what "may I start this work" subtracts, and 061 refused to put it in an index predicate because "an index predicate is a quieter place to put a lifecycle decision than a CHECK constraint, not a weaker one". Question 2 is frozen outside CTR-USG-001 by that contract's own boundary; 1, 3 and 4 have no owner named anywhere but this registry row. §15 forbids an agent closing an open decision, so batch 132 records them and writes no arithmetic. Owed to CTR-USG-001's owners (A0+A6) for OB-008 and to A0/A6 Metering for the other three.

THE ALLOWANCE HALF IS BLOCKED ON FOUR BILLING DECISIONS AS WELL, EACH WITH A DIFFERENT OWNER. NO IDENTITY EXISTS THAT COULD RUN AN ENTITLEMENT RESOLVER, AND A RESOLVER RUN BY `postgres` WOULD PROVE NOTHING. BATCH 132 DECLINES A SERVICE POLICY BATCH 130 EXPECTED IT TO WRITE, AND THE EXPECTATION IS LEFT WHERE IT IS. `db/foundation/lint/read-allowlist.json` DOES NOT EXIST, AND RFC-2026-021 §8.1 REQUIRES IT. So the allowlist is empty by absence rather than by declaration, and the two-way rule §8.2 specifies does not exist in any form. Owed to RFC-2026-021 §8 and to A0, who owns scripts/db/run.mjs. BATCH 170 (2026-10-04, a0-batch-170-assert-plan-2026-10-03.md): PARTLY CLOSED. db/foundation/lint/read-allowlist.json exists as `[]` (§8.1); the read allowlist probe in scripts/db/run.mjs reads §8.2 both ways for client SELECT (every relation anon, authenticated or PUBLIC can SELECT is an allowlist entry or a §8.5 known exception at its level, and every row matches a real grant), with two self-test drifts; batch 132's absence assertion now asserts presence and emptiness. STILL OWED, to A0 (scripts/db/run.mjs) under RFC-2026-021 §8: §8.2's migration-text half (every `create view` in `app` corresponds to an entry; identity-isolation still asserts no migration creates a view), the replacement of the industry-catalog test §8.2 names, §8.3's widening of `exposed_views` in catalog-snapshot.json (draft F8); and the probe reads SELECT only, client INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE being held by the pinned grant probe and the permissive policy probe rather than by this rule (draft F7). The test whose name still says the file is not in the tree is open_blockers[193] (F9). ALSO OWED BEFORE THE FIRST ALLOWLIST ENTRY LANDS (review round): the entry side of the probe's rule 2 checks two of RFC-021 §3's five objects (SELECT on the view, column SELECT on each base table) and not the base table's SELECT policy, schema USAGE, or that the granted columns equal the entry's `columns` (C0 F3; inert while the array is []); and that batch admits its view in the pinned grant probe's first rule, which since the review round names every view, materialized view and foreign table in app and private (A1 R2, Q0 Q-2). The static view regex in identity-isolation now also refuses `create materialized view`.

THE FOUR ISOLATION CASES BATCH 132 ADDS REST ON NO CI NEGATIVE-CONTROL ENTRY, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF A BATCH THAT CREATES NO TABLE. The control step disables row level security on ONE TABLE and requires a failed case matching that table's pattern; batch 132 creates no table, so it adds no entry (batch 041 recorded the same). Two of its four cases are grant-layer refusals, which ci.yml's own comment says "would pass unchanged" with row level security disabled, and the other two name more than one table, so no entry that opens one of them restores either. What holds them instead is the static suite, which pins all four by id, expect, layer and object, and the positive/negative pairing inside the set. app.workspace_entitlements IS CREATED BY NOBODY AND ITS BATCH IS NOT ASSIGNED. §5.1 of the billing contract names the table and calls it recomputable from source; batch 130 declined to create it because "a recomputable projection created by the batch that owns its inputs would be a second source of truth for a value 132 exists to derive"; batch 061 repeated the same from the metering side; and batch 132 declines it because the recompute rule is exactly what the blockers above say does not exist, because it would need a writer (§4's `entitlement-service` module, which does not exist, and RFC-2026-012 §4's command function, which RFC-2026-021 §10 records does not exist), and because §5 gives its family no inventory row. Three batches have now refused it for three compatible reasons and no registry row assigns a fourth, which is the shape RFC-2026-021 §7/3 records for the read allowlist: the batch that would create it is NOT YET ASSIGNED. Owed to A6 Billing and to whoever amends §6's registry.

§6's MIGRATION OWNERSHIP REGISTRY GIVES BATCH 070 THREE WORDS -- "research/evidence/suggestion" -- AND §5's INVENTORY NAMES FIVE OBJECTS, OF WHICH ONE IS IN NEITHER THE REGISTRY NOR §4's ERD. `research.core` is "runs/sources/snapshots/evidence/suggestions"; §4 draws RESEARCH_RUN, RESEARCH_SOURCE, EVIDENCE_ITEM and RESEARCH_SUGGESTION and no snapshot entity at all. Batch 070 creates app.research_snapshots anyway and argues it from three documents that give the row a property no other row in this family has: §9.1 gives it its own sensitivity class (COPYRIGHT-3, where everything else here is CONTENT-2), §10 gives it its own retention class (RESEARCH-SNAPSHOT, 30 days, against RESEARCH-RUN's 12 months) with a final behavior -- "purge object + locator; preserve permitted hash/citation metadata" -- that is one instruction about TWO ROWS WITH DIFFERENT FATES, and §15's DATA-DEC-07 is about it by name. One row cannot half-survive a purge, so folding the capture into app.research_sources would put a COPYRIGHT-3 locator with a thirty-day life in the same row as CONTENT-2 citation metadata with a twelve-month life. THE GAP IS IN §6's REGISTRY AND IN §4's ERD RATHER THAN IN THE MIGRATION, and it is a gap batches have reported before rather than one this batch found: 060 recorded that no registry row anywhere is given a generation-run table and 061 recorded the same about the same table. How many batches have reported it is not counted here -- a count of the batches that share a finding is a claim about the whole schema, and no batch can check one. Owed to A0 and to whoever amends the registry and the ERD.

§8.2 GIVES RESEARCH TWO ROWS THAT LOOK LIKE A CONTRADICTION AND ARE NOT, AND ONLY HALF OF THE FIRST CAN BE IMPLEMENTED. "Start/cancel Research | Y | Y | Y | N | N | P" and "Research run/source/evidence INSERT | N | N | N | N | N | S" are consecutive lines about the same table. Batch 070 reads them as 050 reads §8.4's job pair -- one table, two objects -- so the CANCEL is implemented as a column-scoped client UPDATE behind a policy naming owner, admin and editor, and the START is not, because it is the row's own INSERT and the next line marks that `N` for every client role. Starting research is therefore a COMMAND, RFC-2026-012 §4 names the mechanism (a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by app_command) and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that none exists, so a `Y` cell the matrix grants unconditionally to three roles has no path at all. This is the sharpest form the missing-command-surface debt has taken in this package: earlier batches recorded cells they could not reach because a VIEW was missing or a capability set was undefined; this one is a plain write that a person is entitled to make and cannot. Owed to the batch that brings the command surface and to DATA-DEC-03.

DATA-DEC-07 ("Research snapshot retention, 30 วัน max default, owner Research+Legal, ก่อน real research source") IS OPEN, AND BATCH 070 ENCODES NOTHING, WHICH LEAVES A REAL GAP NAMED HERE RATHER THAN CLOSED. What the schema does is make the decision's absence structural rather than assumed: `app.research_snapshots.retention_until` is NOT NULL with NO DEFAULT and no arithmetic anywhere in the migration, so every capture states its own limit and none inherits a number nobody approved; it is outside every UPDATE grant to every role, so no granted path can push a stated limit forward; the apply-time block refuses a default (read from pg_attribute.atthasdef) and refuses an interval in any CHECK on the five tables; and `purged_at` beside it makes "this repository is holding captured material past its own stated limit" the query `purged_at is null and retention_until < now()` rather than a guess. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS EVERYTHING THAT ACTS ON THAT: there is no sweep (batch 160 owns it), no source-policy mechanism (§10 says the real value is "สั้นกว่าตาม source policy" and nothing in this repository holds a source policy), and no legal-hold table (§10's retention precedence puts a hold first and defines it as hold_type, scope, reason code, created_by, approved_by, start/end/review date and an audit trail -- a subsystem, not a column). Owed to Research+Legal for the number, to batch 160 for the sweep, and to whoever owns the source-policy contract.

app.research_sources IS DECLARED APPEND-ONLY ON BATCH 070's OWN READING RATHER THAN ON A QUOTATION, AND A REVIEWER SHOULD PRESS ON IT. §5's mutability column for research.core reads "mixed; evidence immutable" -- it names ONE of five objects, and the other four are decisions the batch had to make. The argument for the citation is §10's: `RESEARCH-SNAPSHOT`'s final behavior preserves "permitted hash/citation metadata" AFTER the captured object is purged, so the citation is the half that must outlive what it describes, and a citation editable once its snapshot is gone is a claim about a document nobody can check. The cost of being wrong is small and in the safe direction -- nothing can write a source today at all, since §8.2 gives no client INSERT and app_worker holds grants and no policy -- so the disposition decides only what a LATER batch has to do, and adding a grant is a forward migration while removing one after a writer exists is a behaviour change with a data question attached. Owed to A2 Research to countersign or reverse.

THERE IS NO CONTRACT FOR RESEARCH IN THE CONTRACT CATALOG, WHICH CHANGES WHAT A BOUND IN THIS SCHEMA CAN MEAN. `contract-catalog/` holds CTR-JOB-001, CTR-EVT-001, CTR-USG-001, CTR-NTF-001, CTR-AUD-001, CTR-TEN-001, CTR-IDM-001 and the rest, and no CTR-RES-*: batches 050, 051, 061, 131 and 140 could each derive their columns from a frozen envelope and declare their divergences from it, and batch 070 cannot. Two consequences are reported rather than absorbed. FIRST, `app.research_sources.source_uri` HAS NO MAXIMUM LENGTH: 050's rule is that "a CHECK enforcing a bound the contract does not state would make the database stricter than the wire", and no document in this repository bounds a research source URI -- which is also half of why the table has no natural key, because an unbounded text column cannot safely be put in a btree unique index. SECOND, the https-only scheme allowlist and the `..` refusal on that column are BATCH 070's OWN READING of CTR-JOB-001's x-reference-rule (which records an earlier deny-list form accepting file:///etc/passwd, javascript:, //host and traversal) applied to a column a worker will dereference; no document says a research source must be https. Owed to A2 Research and to whoever writes a research envelope.

RFC-2026-022 §3's OWN TABLE DOES NOT CLASSIFY §8.2's `S` CELL, SO BATCH 070 DERIVED THE CLASSIFICATION RATHER THAN CITING ONE, AND THAT DERIVATION SHOULD BE COUNTERSIGNED. §3 names 050, 051, 061, 110, 120, 131 and the asset purge; "Research run/source/evidence INSERT | N N N N N | S" is absent from it. Batch 070 applied §3's own operational test to each of its three statements -- add the confinement term to the WITH CHECK and ask whether the statement still addresses the same work -- and recorded all three as CARRIED in db/foundation/lint/service-policy-map.json with the derivation in each row's `why`: a run's workspace is what the REQUESTER asked about and CTR-TEN-001 makes it server-resolved before the work is enqueued, and a source's and an evidence row's are copied from a run the worker already holds and held to it by a composite foreign key. No service policy is written, because §5/8 puts the whole decision NOT IN EFFECT while the only member of app_worker is postgres. Owed to A1 Security and to the RFC's owner: a classification a batch derived for itself is the case the RFC's §3 table exists to prevent, and the map is where it can be checked.

THREE COLUMNS §4.6 NAMES CARRY NO VOCABULARY AND BATCH 080 INVENTED NONE, WHICH LEAVES THREE FREE-TEXT COLUMNS IN A SCHEMA WHERE EVERY OTHER STATE COLUMN IS CHECKED. §4.6 enumerates `content_items.content_type` (post|carousel|reel), `content_items.status` (seven values), `content_versions.source` (generated|manual|revision), `content_variants.platform` (facebook|instagram), `quality_reviews.status` (pass|warn|block|error) and `quality_reviews.reviewer_type` (ai|human|system) -- six vocabularies, all encoded as CHECKs. It names `content_ideas.status`, `content_items.approval_state` and `content_variants.variant_type` AND ENUMERATES NOTHING FOR THEM. The columns exist, because §4.6 names them and adding a column to an immutable table later is worse than a column with no CHECK; they carry no CHECK, because a vocabulary written here would be this batch choosing one for Product -- the ownership irregularity WP-0A-CON-006 records as High against CTR-NTF-001. `approval_state` is the sharpest of the three: §4.7 gives `approval_requests.status` a vocabulary and that is a DIFFERENT COLUMN on a table batch 090 owns, so the obvious borrowing is the one thing a reader must not do. Owed to Product and to A3 Content, and to batch 090 for the second.

app.content_ideas REFERENCES app.research_suggestions ON `id` ALONE, WHICH IS WEAKER THAN EVERY OTHER CROSS-FAMILY REFERENCE IN THIS SCHEMA, AND THE FIX IS OWED TO BATCH 070's OWNER. Every child in batch 070 reaches its parent over the whole scope path -- `foreign key (workspace_id, business_profile_id, research_run_id) references app.research_runs (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id)` -- which is what makes a child's own Workspace and Business the ones its parent actually has (§4 invariant 10). app.research_suggestions exposes no such key: measured on the provisioned schema, its only unique constraint is `PRIMARY KEY (id)`. A scope-path foreign key into it is therefore impossible, and adding the composite unique it would need is a change to a table batch 070 owns, which ownership forbids this batch from making. SO THE REFERENCE GUARANTEES THE SUGGESTION EXISTS AND DOES NOT GUARANTEE IT BELONGS TO THE CITING TENANT. Row level security still prevents READING the other tenant's suggestion; what is unprotected is a dangling cross-tenant citation written by a caller that already holds the id. The fixture deliberately loads no such row, so nothing here makes the gap look closed. Owed to A2 Research for `unique (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id)` on app.research_suggestions, and to A3 Content for the forward migration that tightens the key once it exists.

THE `findings` CHECK HOLDS A SHAPE AND CANNOT HOLD THE THREE THINGS §4.6 ACTUALLY ASKS FOR. §4.6: "finding \u0e15\u0e49\u0e2d\u0e07\u0e21\u0e35 stable rule code \u0e41\u0e25\u0e30 user-facing Thai message". quality_reviews_findings_carry_code_and_message requires every element to be an object with a non-empty string `rule_code` and a non-empty string `message_th`, written as jsonpath because Postgres refuses a subquery in a CHECK with 0A000. IT DOES NOT HOLD: that `message_th` is in Thai, that `rule_code` is STABLE across rule-set versions, or that a whitespace-only string is rejected -- jsonpath has no trim, so `" "` passes a constraint whose whole purpose is that a person sees a message. The first two are owed to whoever owns the rule set; THE THIRD IS A REAL GAP IN THIS CONSTRAINT, reported rather than papered over, and the forward fix is a trigger or a generated column, neither of which this batch is entitled to invent for a table §8.2 marks immutable. Owed to A3 Content.

NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN WRITE A CONTENT VERSION, A VARIANT OR A QUALITY REVIEW, AND THAT IS §8.2 ROW 3 FOLLOWED RATHER THAN A LIMITATION OF THE BATCH. "Approved/published version UPDATE/DELETE" is `N` for owner, admin, editor, approver, viewer AND service -- the only row in §8's four matrices that is `N` in every column -- so the three tables carry no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE grant to any role and no policy for any of those verbs, asserted both ways against the live catalog. The writer they wait for is a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by `app_command`, and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that no command function exists anywhere in this repository. [CORRECTED 2026-09-15 by batch 082: this entry first read "exempt by OWNERSHIP rather than by privilege (RFC-2026-017 §3)", which is FALSE and was found so independently by C0 and A1 — 001_service_roles.sql:41-42 creates app_command NOBYPASSRLS and never the table owner PRECISELY so the policies apply to it, and RFC-2026-017 §3 says such a function "is subject to RLS and needs policies that name it — which is the intended behaviour". The same false sentence stands uneditable at 080_content.sql:114 and :897; 082's header carries the correction. What the false sentence licensed is finding S8 below.] THE CONSEQUENCE IS LARGER HERE THAN IN THE BATCHES THAT RECORDED IT BEFORE: content generation is the product, and the tables that hold what was generated cannot receive a row. Batch 080 deliberately does NOT grant app_worker the verbs as a stopgap -- that would be a second path to an act RFC-2026-017 §3 gives to a command function, which is the shape RFC-2026-018 was superseded for proposing. Owed to DATA-DEC-03, to the batch that brings the command surface, and to A3 Content.

§8.2's "Content create/edit/version" IS `Y` FOR THREE ROLES AND IS IMPLEMENTED IN HALF, WITH THE MISSING HALF NAMED. A client may create a content item, rename it and soft-delete it; a client may NOT move `status` from `draft` to `approved`, because §4.6 says "state change \u0e1c\u0e48\u0e32\u0e19 domain command; \u0e2b\u0e49\u0e32\u0e21 client update status \u0e2d\u0e34\u0e2a\u0e23\u0e30" and the column is outside every UPDATE grant.
