This batch CITES that disposition rather than re-asking it, and records the consequence: a `Y` cell three roles hold has no path for half of what it grants until a command function exists. Owed to the same batch the blocker above names.

app.generation_runs IS STILL ASSIGNED TO NOBODY, AND BATCH 080 NOW HOLDS TWO COLUMNS THAT REFERENCE IT. `content_versions.generation_run_id` and `quality_reviews.generation_run_id` carry no foreign key: the table exists nowhere and §6's 000-180 registry gives it to no batch, which batch 060 recorded and batch 061 recorded after it. The Product Owner disposed the question on 2026-09-10 (evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/product-owner-disposition-generation-run.md, option \u0e01): keep the columns as references with no foreign key, batch 131's precedent for a reference whose target is absent. WHAT THAT COSTS IS UNCHANGED BY BEING APPROVED: nothing enforces the reference until a command function exists, so a generation_run_id may name a run that never existed, and `content_versions` is immutable -- a value written now cannot be tightened without a forward migration. The fixture writes NULL in both columns rather than a plausible uuid, so nothing in this repository makes the unenforced reference look like a working one. Owed to A0 and to whoever amends §6's registry.

SHAPE B IS OWED: THE CONTENT COMMAND WRITER IS STILL UNBOUNDED BY DESIGN, AND BATCH 082 ONLY CLOSES THE PATH. A1 finding S8 (evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-security-batch-080-2026-09-13.md §2A, stop-the-line): 080's five scope narrowings are `for all to authenticated` and bind no other role, so the SECURITY DEFINER function running as app_command that 080 waits for would be constrained by nothing but its own permissive policy. Product Owner decision Q3 (product-owner-disposition-2026-09-15-six-questions.md): shape C now, shape B afterwards. 082 is shape C — one RESTRICTIVE policy per table, FOR ALL, TO PUBLIC, `current_user = 'authenticated'` — which refuses every non-authenticated role every row until a batch amends it in a reviewed diff. It decides NOTHING about how the command writer should be scoped. Shape B — a narrowing that asks the member-scope question about the ACTING USER the command serves, read from a session setting through a helper taking the user as a parameter, failing closed when the setting is absent — changes the RLS semantics of a service path and needs a contract for how the command path carries the acting user; CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md requires an RFC for both. Shape A — naming app_command in a narrowing that uses 080's predicate — was measured VACUOUS (021_member_scope.sql:389-400 is security invoker over a table app_command sees zero rows of, so it reports "not narrowed" and admits everything) and must not be taken. Owed to the first batch that writes a content command function, as an RFC, before that batch touches 082's closure. [2026-09-15, integration of 081: the nine role runs found the same S8 shape in 081, 090 and 100 (A1-081 S1 measured it live on a scratch PostgreSQL 17.11: with a permissive INSERT policy naming app_command, the role wrote targets under tenant B's item while 082 refused the identical shape on content_items). Each batch integrates with a closure file of its own -- 083 for content_targets, 092 for approval, 101 for asset -- of 082's exact shape, held to it by one static rule (SERVICE_PATH_CLOSURES in identity-isolation.test.mjs). Shape B is now owed for all four families, and it is one RFC, not four.] [2026-09-15, later: DRAFTED as architecture/decisions/RFC-2026-023-acting-user-narrowing.md, Status: In review -- acting-user helpers owned by app_authz reading the request claims, fail closed on no claims, the closure amended to admit app_command only through them, proven by two cases per closed table under a SECURITY DEFINER function. The Owner disposes; the blocker closes when the RFC is approved AND a batch lands it.]

CLOSED 2026-09-15 BY A0, WITH THE CEILING ITSELF: the byte budget and MAX_ARG_STRLEN no longer exist in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs, so 131 has no margin to be under. app.content_targets.status CARRIES NO VOCABULARY AND BATCH 081 INVENTED NONE, WHICH MAKES IT THE FOURTH FREE-TEXT STATE COLUMN IN content.core. §4.6 lists the target's columns as "`id`, scope, `content_item_id`, `social_account_id`, `content_variant_id`, `status`" and enumerates NOTHING for the last of them, exactly as it does for `content_ideas.status`, `content_items.approval_state` and `content_variants.variant_type` -- the three batch 080 left unchecked and recorded. The column exists, because §4.6 names it; it carries a SHAPE constraint only (a whitespace-only status is refused) and no CHECK on its values, because a vocabulary written in a migration would be this batch choosing one for Product -- the ownership irregularity WP-0A-CON-006 records as High against CTR-NTF-001. The sharpest trap is the one §4.7 sets: `approval_requests.status` has five values (pending|approved|changes_requested|cancelled|expired) and that is a DIFFERENT COLUMN on a table batch 090 owns, so the obvious borrowing is the one thing a reader must not do. A static rule asserts that no value from any neighbouring vocabulary appears anywhere in 081_content_targets.sql. Owed to Product and to A3 Content, and to batch 090 for the second half.

§4.6's "UNIQUE ACTIVE TARGET" IS IMPLEMENTED OVER `deleted_at` RATHER THAN OVER `status`, WHICH IS STRICTER THAN THE RULE AS STATED, AND THE SUBSTITUTION IS BATCH 081's OWN DERIVATION. Which status values are ACTIVE is exactly the vocabulary the blocker above records as undecided, so the rule §4.6 states cannot be written at all. content_targets_active_destination is therefore `unique (content_item_id, social_account_id) where deleted_at is null`: every row §4.6 would call active is a row with a null `deleted_at`, so nothing §4.6 forbids is permitted -- BUT a target whose status a future vocabulary would call `cancelled`, and which has not been soft-deleted, STILL OCCUPIES THE SLOT, so a legitimate second target for the same destination is refused until the first is retired. STRICT IS THE DIRECTION THIS BATCH CHOSE ON PURPOSE: a duplicate live target for one content item and one destination is the shape of a double post, and CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS makes publishing idempotency non-negotiable, so the failure a reader will complain about was preferred to the one nobody notices until it has posted twice. The forward fix once the vocabulary exists is a partial index over the active values. Owed to Product, who owns the vocabulary, and to whoever countersigns a rule a batch derived for itself -- which is the same shape batch 070 recorded when it derived an RFC-2026-022 §3 classification the RFC's own table did not carry.

§4.6's "TARGET PIN IMMUTABLE VERSION ก่อน APPROVE/SCHEDULE" IS HALF WRITABLE AND THE UNWRITABLE HALF IS THE CONDITIONAL. `content_variant_id` is nullable, because §4.6's own sentence says the pin happens BEFORE approve/schedule and therefore that an unpinned target is a state a target passes through. The other half -- pinned BY THE TIME the status is approved or scheduled -- is a CHECK naming status values nobody has decided, so it is not written and NOTHING STOPS AN UNPINNED TARGET REACHING ANY STATE. The consequence is not cosmetic: an approver would be approving a destination with no content pinned to it, which is the case §4.7's "request pin content version" exists to prevent one table over. The forward fix is a CHECK once the vocabulary exists, or a trigger, and this batch is entitled to neither. Owed to Product beside the blocker above.

THE PIN IS HELD TO THE TENANT AND THE BUSINESS AND NOT TO THIS TARGET'S OWN CONTENT ITEM, AND THE FIX IS A FORWARD MIGRATION BECAUSE BATCH 080 IS MERGED. content_targets_variant_scope_fk reaches app.content_variants over (workspace_id, business_profile_id, content_variant_id), so a variant from another tenant or another Business is refused by the database and the isolation suite proves it with a 23503 case. What nothing enforces is that the pinned variant is a variant of a version of `content_item_id`: a variant hangs off a version and the VERSION carries the item, so the key that would say it needs a unique constraint on app.content_variants spanning the item -- and app.content_variants carries no `content_item_id` column at all. Postgres refuses a subquery in a CHECK with 0A000 (batch 080 recorded the same wall on its `findings` constraint), and §6 invariant 1 forbids rewriting a merged migration, so the repair is a forward migration that adds the column and the key to 080's table and then tightens this one. SO A TARGET MAY PIN A VARIANT OF A DIFFERENT CONTENT ITEM IN THE SAME BUSINESS, which is a wrong post rather than a leak. The fixture pins only variants of each target's own item, so nothing here makes the gap look closed. Owed to A3 Content.

CLOSED 2026-09-15 BY BATCH 111 (A0 Integration, §6 registry): content_targets_social_scope_fk (workspace_id, social_account_id) -> app.social_accounts (workspace_id, id), with social_accounts_scope_key added for it and a supporting index; the three destination symbols retired for social_account_a1/a2/b1 with fixed ids in 110's fixture; editor-a-cannot-aim-a-content-target-at-another-tenants-destination refused 23503. [ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS] app.content_targets.social_account_id CARRIES NO FOREIGN KEY AT ALL, BY §6's REGISTRY, AND THE COLUMN IS RESOLVED AGAINST NOTHING WHATSOEVER. §6 gives "business-channel/social FK" to batch 111 (A0 Integration, depending on 110, 020 and 081) and gives batch 081 the "target placeholder contract"; the workstream registry spells the same row "deferred Social FK prepared". app.social_accounts EXISTS on disk in 110_meta_connector.sql, so this key is WITHHELD rather than impossible, which is why 081_content_targets.sql asserts its ABSENCE against pg_constraint at apply time -- a deferral nobody can check is indistinguishable from an omission, and the day somebody writes the key here instead of in 111 the migration fails rather than quietly performing another batch's deliverable. WHAT IT COSTS UNTIL 111 LANDS: nothing checks that a destination exists, and nothing checks that it belongs to the Workspace the target is in. Row level security cannot help, because there is no parent for a policy to ask about. A caller holding another tenant's social account id can write it into its own target and the database will accept it. THERE IS ALSO A REPOINTING DEBT: `content_target_destination_a1`, `_a2` and `_b1` in db/foundation/seeds/fixture-catalog.json are uuids that name NO ROW -- deliberately, so the fixture does not make the unenforced reference look like a working one -- and the day batch 111 adds the key, tests/db/identity/fixtures/081-content-targets-fixture.sql STOPS LOADING until all three are repointed at social accounts that exist. That failure is intended and is stated in the fixture header, in the catalog and here, so 111's author meets it three times before CI does. Owed to A0 Integration.

WHICH ROW OF §8 GOVERNS A CONTENT TARGET IS BATCH 081's READING AND NOT A CITATION, AND IT DECIDES WHAT AN EDITOR MAY DO. This batch applies §8.2's content rows -- "Content SELECT | Y Y Y Y Y | P" and "Content create/edit/version | Y Y Y N N | P" -- because §4.6 places `content_targets` in `content.core`. The competing reading is §8.3's "Schedule/unschedule | Y | Y | P | N | N | P", under which an EDITOR is `P` -- "ผ่านตาม policy/explicit capability" -- and no document in this repository defines that capability, so an editor would hold NOTHING on this table. The ground for the reading is §4.7's own inventory: `content_schedules` is a SEPARATE table carrying `content_target_id`, `scheduled_for` and a timezone snapshot, and it belongs to batch 091 -- choosing a destination is not scheduling a post to it, and §8.3's verb lands on the schedule row. If the reading is wrong, the case that has to change is named: `editor-a-can-aim-a-content-target-inside-their-narrowing`. Owed to whoever owns the §8 matrix and to A5, who owns 091 and will meet the same question from the other side.

NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN RE-PIN, RE-AIM OR RE-HOME A CONTENT TARGET, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN FOLLOWED RATHER THAN A LIMITATION OF THE BATCH. `content_variant_id`, `social_account_id` and `content_item_id` are outside every UPDATE grant to every role, asserted per column against the live ACL at apply time: a pin the pinner can move afterwards is not a pin (§4.6), and re-aiming a target at another item or another destination is CREATING a different target, which §8.5 also forbids as moving a row across scope with an update. The act those three columns are waiting for is the same SECURITY DEFINER function owned by app_command that batch 080's three immutable tables wait for, and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that no command function exists anywhere in this repository. Batch 081 deliberately does NOT grant app_worker the verbs as a stopgap -- that would be the second path RFC-2026-018 was superseded for proposing -- so every service case on this table is a PRIVILEGE refusal, none carries RFC-2026-017 §7, and none is in the CI negative control's basis. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NARROWER THAN 080's AND STILL REAL: a client may create a target and retire it, and a mistake in either of the three fixed columns can only be corrected by retiring the row and creating another. Owed to DATA-DEC-03, to the batch that brings the command surface, and to A3 Content.

`app.approval_policy_steps` IS NAMED BY §4.7 AND GIVEN TO NO BATCH BY §6, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME SITUATION BATCH 080 REPORTED AND IS WORSE. §4.7 heads its first approval bullet "`approval_policies` / `approval_policy_steps`" and says of the second half "steps มีลำดับ, action type, required role". No row in §6's 000-180 registry names a step table, §5's inventory lists three objects and not four, and batch 091 -- the only later batch in this family -- is "calendar/schedule". Batch 080 refused `content_targets` on the same rule and that table went to a NAMED later batch, 081; this one goes nowhere. The consequence is already in the schema: `app.approval_events.step` carries §4.7's ordinal with NO foreign key and no referent, so a step number can name a step that never existed, and app.approval_events is append-only -- a value written now cannot be tightened without a forward migration. Owed to A0 and to whoever amends §6's registry.

§4.7 NAMES `approval_events.action` AND ENUMERATES NOTHING, so the column carries no CHECK. §8.3's third row is "Approve/reject/request changes", which is a matrix row about who may act and not an alphabet of strings a row may hold; a CHECK derived from it would be batch 090 choosing the event vocabulary for Product, which is the ownership irregularity WP-0A-CON-006 records as High against CTR-NTF-001. The fixture loads `fixture-action-*` strings rather than `approve` or `reject`, so nothing in this repository makes an invented vocabulary look like a decided one. This is the same shape as batch 080's three unenumerated columns and it is the ONLY one batch 090 has, because §4.7 supplies `approval_requests.status` in full. Owed to Product.

§4.7 AND §5 DISAGREE ABOUT THE SCOPE OF AN APPROVAL POLICY, AND BATCH 090 RESOLVED IT BY PRECEDENCE RATHER THAN BY JUDGEMENT -- WHICH MEANS A PRODUCT CAPABILITY IS NOW INEXPRESSIBLE. §4.7: "Policy อยู่ Workspace หรือ Business scope". §5 of the sprint-0a document gives `approval.core` the Scope "business/page". Those describe different tables: the first makes `business_profile_id` nullable, the second makes it mandatory with a Page override. §2 of the sprint-0a document ranks itself above `core-database-and-rls-workstream-th.md` ("เอกสารนี้ > workstream เดิม", item 5 in its own list), so §5 wins and the column is NOT NULL. THE COST: a workspace-wide approval policy cannot be written, and a product that wants one needs a Business-scoped row per Business, kept in step by nothing. If §4.7 is the intended shape the fix is a forward migration and an amendment to §5, not an edit here -- migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting a merged migration. Owed to A5 Workflow and to whoever amends §5.

`approval_requests.status` CARRIES FIVE VALUES AND NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN WRITE THE FIFTH. §4.7 gives "pending|approved|changes_requested|cancelled|expired" and the CHECK quotes all five. §8.3 has NO ROW that produces `expired`: the create/cancel row writes `cancelled`, the approve/reject row writes the other two, `pending` is the column default, and the Service column on all three rows is `P` with no capability defined anywhere. No document in this repository states how long an approval request stays open, so a default interval in the migration would have been batch 090 setting a product deadline -- which is what batch 070 refused to do for DATA-DEC-07's retention number. The absence is ASSERTED rather than left to be noticed: 090_approval.sql fails at apply time if any policy's WITH CHECK half mentions `expired`, and `owner-a-cannot-expire-an-approval-request` asserts it at run time from the one identity that holds both write paths. A request that should expire cannot. Owed to Product, with the window and the actor both needed.

NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN WRITE AN APPROVAL EVENT, SO A DECISION CAN BE TAKEN AND NOT RECORDED. §8.3 row 4 -- "Approval event UPDATE/DELETE" -- is `N` for owner, admin, editor, approver, viewer AND service, which only §8.2 row 3 is besides it, and batch 090 implements it as absent grants and absent policies asserted both ways. INSERT is absent too, on a reading rather than a quotation: §8.3's row names UPDATE and DELETE, §4.7 says the trail is append-only and "decision ห้าม update/delete", and a decision trail a client can author proves nothing about the decision -- so the writer is a SECURITY DEFINER command function owned by app_command (RFC-2026-017 §3) and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that none exists. THIS IS WORSE THAN BATCH 080's EQUIVALENT AND NOT EQUIVALENT TO IT: 080 left a table nothing could write and nothing could read meaningfully either, while batch 090 leaves a table whose PARENT is fully writable. A client can raise, cancel and decide a request through the policies batch 090 writes, and §4 invariant 8's immutable "Approval/Usage/Audit history" stays empty while they do. §8.3 MARKS ADMIN AND EDITOR `P` ON "Approve/reject/request changes" AND BATCH 090 REFUSES BOTH, BECAUSE THE CAPABILITY THAT WOULD MAKE `P` MEAN SOMETHING IS DEFINED NOWHERE. `P` is "ผ่านตาม policy/explicit capability". `app.approval_policies.required_role` is the nearest thing in the schema to that policy -- batch 090 creates the column, with §7's five role values as a CHECK -- and NO POLICY PREDICATE IN THE MIGRATION READS IT, because nothing states what reading it would mean: whether a matching `required_role` grants the decide path, whether `minimum_approvers` is counted by the database or by a command, or what happens when a policy version is disabled. §8.3 HAS NO SELECT ROW FOR APPROVAL POLICY, REQUEST OR EVENT, SO THE CLIENT READ SURFACE BATCH 090 WRITES IS A READING AND NOT AN IMPLEMENTED CELL. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN WRITE AN app.asset_versions ROW OR SET app.assets.current_version_id, SO §8.2's "Asset upload" `Y` IS IMPLEMENTED IN HALF. An upload creates an asset AND its first version; §5 makes the version immutable, so its creation is not a client act and no client role holds INSERT on it, while `app_worker` holds the INSERT grant and no policy and row level security refuses it. `current_version_id` is outside every INSERT grant (no version exists when the asset is inserted) and outside every UPDATE grant (which version is CURRENT is the act of publishing one, not a field a client edits -- 080's sentence about a content item), so it is permanently NULL. Both halves wait on a SECURITY DEFINER command function owned by `app_command`, which RFC-2026-021 §10 records does not exist. This is the shape the Product Owner accepted for batch 070 on 2026-09-10 (question 1) and for batch 080; it is CITED rather than re-asked, and the consequence is recorded plainly: a tenant can create an asset with no media in it and nothing can give it any.

§4 INVARIANT 5 PUTS TWO CONDITIONS ON A PIN AND THIS SCHEMA ENFORCES NEITHER. "Content/Publish ที่ใช้สื่อต้อง pin `asset_version_id` ที่ `ready` และ rights valid", and §6.2 of the asset design repeats both for the attach path. app.content_asset_links enforces the PIN -- a composite foreign key holds the version to the asset named beside it -- and cannot enforce either condition: `ready` is a lifecycle state on another table, which a CHECK cannot read and a policy could only read through the coupling batch 020 rejects; `rights valid` is a state app.asset_rights carries per asset with nothing binding it to the instant the link is made, and §2.2's ERD lets one asset carry several rights records. A reader who takes the foreign key for the invariant has taken it for more than it is. Owed to the command surface and to A4.

`pg_trgm` IS NOT IN BATCH 000's APPROVED EXTENSION SET, SO §5.1's REQUIRED THAI-SEARCH INDEX CANNOT BE BUILT AND THE COLUMN IT WOULD INDEX IS ABSENT. §5.1 of the asset design lists "GIN trigram บน `assets.search_text`" among the indexes that must exist FROM THE FIRST MIGRATION, and batch 000 creates `pgcrypto` and nothing else. THE PRODUCT COST IS REAL AND IS NOT A SCHEMA PREFERENCE: the asset library is specified as a Thai-language, mobile-first search-and-filter surface, and it has no text index at all. Owed to A0 and to an RFC amending batch 000's approved set.

§5.1's "RIGHTS EXPIRY NOTIFICATION" SWEEP HAS AN INDEX AND NO WRITER. The index exists -- `asset_rights(workspace_id, business_profile_id, expires_at) where rights_status in ('valid','expiring')` -- and nothing can move a row through it: §8 has no `S` cell anywhere for a rights row, so `app_worker` holds SELECT on app.asset_rights and no INSERT and no UPDATE, and where a document is silent the cell is denied (030's reading, kept by 050, 060, 061, 070, 110 and 131). §6.2's "Audit ทุกครั้ง" ON A RIGHTS CHANGE IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, AND `created_by` IS THEREFORE THE ONLY RECORD OF WHO ASSERTED A LICENCE. §6.2 of the asset design attaches an audit requirement to exactly one row of its own policy matrix -- "Change rights/share | Owner/Admin; Approver เมื่อ policy อนุญาต | Audit ทุกครั้ง" -- and binding an audit record to the act it describes is what a command function is for. THE SHARING PATH IS UNIMPLEMENTED AND UNOWNED, AND IT IS THE REFUSAL IN BATCH 100 A REVIEWER SHOULD PRESS HARDEST ON. §6.2 admits a reader who has "สิทธิ์ Business/Page หรือ Asset ถูกแชร์อย่างชัดเจน", §4.7 allows a link across Businesses "เว้นแต่ Asset ถูก Admin share", and §4.1 gives `assets.scope` a third value `workspace_shared`. So batch 100 creates no share table, encodes no `scope` column (two of its three values restate `page_context_profile_id` and the third IS this decision), and makes "same Business" unconditional. THE CLIENT WRITES A PUBLISH INTENT AND RFC-2026-012's INVENTORY SAYS THE SERVICE SHOULD. Its line for this family reads "publish intents/targets/posts/metrics | view only | INSERT service-only; PROVIDER-3", and its decision 1 is "Server-only mutation for every table family in §5, zero exceptions". Batch 120 grants `authenticated` INSERT and a three-column UPDATE on app.publish_intents, on §8.3's "Publish now/cancel pending" `Y` for the owner and the admin, and on the precedent of batches 081 and 090, which read `authenticated` as the user's server session rather than as a browser (RFC-2026-012 §2's own framing). The Product Owner took that reading on 2026-09-15 (question 14) knowing it departs from an approved RFC's inventory line. Owed to RFC-2026-012's owners as a correction to the inventory or to this batch as a forward fix.

app.publish_intents HAS NO `status` COLUMN AND §4.8 NAMES ONE, SO "CANCEL PENDING" IS NOT A DATABASE RULE. §8.3's verb is "Publish now/cancel PENDING" and §4.8 lists `status` among the intent's columns. Batch 120 creates none, on the Product Owner's answer to question 5b of 2026-09-15, because under this batch's grants no role could move it: the client's UPDATE is the cancellation and app_worker holds SELECT alone. An intent's state is therefore what its targets say, and a cancellation is accepted whatever those targets already did -- a send that has already published can have its intent cancelled and nothing refuses it. Owed to the command surface, and to batch 091, which carries `publish_intent_id` on a schedule and will meet the same question from the other side.

TWO VOCABULARIES NAME ONE DISTINCTION AND NOTHING RECONCILES THEM. app.published_posts.platform and app.content_variants.platform and app.content_asset_links.platform carry `facebook`/`instagram` (batches 080, 100, 120); app.social_accounts.account_kind carries `fb`/`ig` (batch 110). Both are `text` + a named CHECK per §3.2 and both are the document's own tokens -- §4's relation invariant 7 names "FB และ IG" and §4.6 names the longer pair -- so neither is wrong and a third spelling would be worse. NOTHING HOLDS THEM IN STEP: a publish target may pin an `instagram` variant while naming a `fb` account, and no constraint in this schema refuses it, because the two columns are three tables apart and a CHECK cannot read another row. Batch 120's fixture and its fan-out cases keep them consistent deliberately, so that no case demonstrates the gap as though it were a feature. Owed to the command surface and to whoever reconciles §4.6's vocabulary with §4's.

A SEND CARRIES NO SOFT LIFECYCLE AND §3.2 ASKS EVERY MUTABLE ROW FOR ONE. §3.2: "Soft lifecycle: archived_at หรือ deleted_at; hard delete ผ่าน retention job เท่านั้น". app.publish_intents, app.publish_targets and app.publish_jobs are mutable and carry neither. The reading batch 120 took: publish history is kept for the life of the Workspace (§10, PUBLISH-HISTORY), its removal is batch 160's at closure under §11.4's ordered purge, and a `deleted_at` a client could set would be a way to hide a delivery from the export §11.1 requires. THE COST IS THAT NOTHING CAN BE RETIRED: an intent created by mistake stays, and its only lifecycle is `cancelled_at`. Owed to batch 160 and to Product.

ONE JOB PER SEND IS BATCH 120's READING OF §4.8 AND MAKES §4.8's OWN UNIQUENESS RULE MOOT. §4.8 gives publish_jobs "target_id, kernel_job_id, status, attempt summary, provider_request_key" and the rule "provider request key unique ต่อ target" -- a per-target uniqueness that presupposes more than one row per target can exist. Batch 120 makes `publish_target_id` UNIQUE, on the technical architecture's "แต่ละการส่งไปหนึ่ง Social Account สร้าง publish_target และ publish_job แยกกัน" and on batch 050's scalar-attempt model, so retries are attempts on one row and §4.8's rule is guaranteed by the structure rather than enforced by a key. The key that IS written is broader -- `unique (workspace_id, provider_request_key)` -- because two sends sharing a provider key would have the provider fold two publications into one, which is the double post's mirror image. Both departures are readings. Owed to A6 Publisher.

§4 INVARIANT 5's TWO CONDITIONS ARE UNENFORCED ON A PUBLISH TARGET'S ASSET PIN, EXACTLY AS THEY ARE ON A CONTENT ASSET LINK. "Content/Publish ที่ใช้สื่อต้อง pin `asset_version_id` ที่ `ready` และ rights valid" -- and app.publish_target_assets enforces the PIN (a composite key holds the version to the asset named beside it and to the tenant and Business) and neither condition: `ready` is a lifecycle state on another table a CHECK cannot read, and rights are a state app.asset_rights carries per asset with nothing binding it to the instant of the pin. This is the blocker batch 100 recorded for app.content_asset_links, word for word, on a second table. Owed to the command surface and to A4.

BATCH 091 DID NOT EXIST WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN, AND §6's REGISTRY DEPENDS 120 ON IT. (Since 2026-09-28 batch 091 exists -- PR #164, A0 writing it on the Owner's decision -- and 124 adds content_schedules.publish_intent_id's key to publish_intents; the open part below is unchanged and is carried into the batch 091 blocker's item (g).) The dependency is satisfiable in the direction the documents actually point: §4.7 gives `content_schedules` a `publish_intent_id`, so 091 references 120 and not the other way round, and batch 120 names no table 091 will create. WHAT IS LEFT OPEN is the state `request_kind = 'scheduled'` describes: an intent may declare itself scheduled and there is no schedule row anywhere to say when, and nothing refuses the combination. One fixture intent carries that value so the CHECK is exercised rather than merely declared. Owed to A5, who owns 091 -- and who will also meet §8.3's "Schedule/unschedule" row, which batch 081 read as belonging to 091 rather than to a content target.

THE EDITOR'S PUBLISHING CAPABILITY IS UNDEFINED AND BATCH 120 REFUSES THE EDITOR ON THAT GROUND, WHICH IS A DECISION AND NOT A CITATION. §8.3's "Publish now/cancel pending" marks the editor `P` -- "ผ่านตาม policy/explicit capability" -- and no document in this repository defines that capability. This repository holds TWO shapes for a client `P` and they point opposite ways: REFUSED where nothing defines it (070's approver, 090's admin and editor on approve/reject, 110's owner cells) and IMPLEMENTED as a conditional grant where an explicit member scope IS the capability (021's `*_scoped_editor` policies, 030's industry assignment; tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs pins that reading -- "an absent scope row is not explicit"). §5.1 of the core-database workstream ties an editor's publishing to "เมื่อ policy อนุญาตและ approved", which is an APPROVAL condition rather than a scope one, so the 021 shape would have implemented half of that sentence and read as the whole of it. The Product Owner chose the refusal on 2026-09-15 (question 2 of product-owner-disposition-2026-09-15-batch-120.md). THE CASE THAT CHANGES IF THE READING IS EVER REVERSED IS NAMED: `editor-a-cannot-request-a-publish-intent`, and the editor's READ of the same row is asserted beside it so the refusal is about the operation and not the table. Owed to whoever owns the §8 matrix and to Product: either a capability definition, or §5.1's approval condition expressed in something the database can evaluate. [Recorded 2026-09-15 after C0's finding M2 on batch 120: 120_publisher.sql's header claimed this blocker existed before it did.]

THE RAW EXTERNAL IDENTIFIER OF A PROVIDER OBJECT STILL HAS NO HOME, AND BATCH 120 IS THE BATCH BATCH 110 SAID WOULD ANSWER. 110_meta_connector.sql and open_blockers' batch 110 entry both end "Owed to the batch that brings the typed service AND TO 120, which is the first batch with a caller that has to address a Page at the provider" -- so this entry is that debt inherited rather than a new one, and it now covers TWO values instead of one: the external ACCOUNT identifier §9.3 asks for beside its hash, and the external POST identifier §4.8 names on a published post. WHY IT IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN SOLVED, in the two sentences batch 110 used and which are both still true: an encrypted form needs a mechanism no decision in this repository names (§9.3's other encryption requirements are platform-level), and a private form needs a reference reachable only through the typed service, which does not exist. The tables 060 and 110 put in `private` hold LOCATORS -- "never the value, never a ciphertext of the value" -- so a plaintext column there would be a new pattern rather than their shape, and the Product Owner was given that option on 2026-09-15 (question 6) and chose the deferral.

THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO NOBODY DISCOVERS IT: until the debt is paid, nothing can address a Page at the provider and no app.published_posts row can be produced by anything but a fixture -- which is the state every `S` cell in this schema is already in for RFC-2026-022 §5/8's reason, so the debt costs nothing TODAY and is the first thing the batch that brings the worker must pay. Owed to the typed service and to DATA-DEC-03 (due before G1). [Recorded 2026-09-15 after A1's finding F2 on batch 120: 120_publisher.sql's header said the debt "stays open in the work package" before an entry carried it.]

THE SERVICE CANNOT RESOLVE THE POST WHOSE METRICS IT IS TO COLLECT, SO THE STATEMENT BATCH 121 CLASSIFIES CARRIED CANNOT BE COMPOSED BY THE SERVICE AT ALL. Measured 2026-09-16 on a scratch cluster: as app_worker, `select count(*) from app.published_posts` returns ZERO, and so do app.publish_targets and app.publish_intents. Batch 120 grants app_worker SELECT on the post and writes it NO POLICY, because RFC-2026-022 is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8), and a granted read with no policy reads nothing.

WHY THAT IS WORSE HERE THAN IT LOOKS. RFC-2026-022 §3 classifies this cell CARRIED on the ground that the workspace is an INPUT -- `published_post_id` is a parameter the server resolved before forming the statement -- and batch 121's own register entry gives that reasoning in full. It is correct about the STATEMENT and it is silent about where the parameter comes from: there is no path in this database by which the service obtains a post id. A collector cannot ask "which posts are due a reading" because it can see no posts.

This is the same finding the fifth pass recorded against batch 120's fan-out -- app_worker refused app.content_targets and app.content_variants, so the send §8.3 marks `S` cannot be composed either -- one table further down, and it now covers EVERY statement of the publishing `S` cell. The four CARRIED classifications in service-policy-map.json are claims about statements that no service in this schema can currently form. Owed to the batch that brings the command surface, and to RFC-2026-022 §7.

§8.3 HAS NO SELECT ROW FOR A METRIC, AND THE CLIENT READ BATCH 121 GRANTS IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A CITATION. The matrix gives publishing exactly two rows -- "Publish now/cancel pending" and "Publish delivery/post/metric INSERT" -- and neither is a read. Batch 120 met this for the intent, the send, the job and the post and recorded it (blocker 146's shape); batch 121 meets it for the metric and records it SEPARATELY rather than as an inheritance, because the reasons differ. The Product Owner's answer to question E of 2026-09-16 grants a column-scoped SELECT to active members narrowed through the item, on the ground that §11.1 puts publish history in the PDPA export minimum and DB-10's acceptance requires partial success to be SHOWN.

WHAT MAKES IT SHARPER ON THIS TABLE THAN ON THE OTHER FOUR: the intent, the send, the job and the post are records of what the system DID and have a use even if no client ever reads them. A metric has none. If §8 is later read as refusing the client read, this table has no purpose and should not exist -- so the decision is load-bearing for the table itself and not only for its projection. Owed to whoever amends §8.3.

NOTHING ENFORCES THE COLLECTION CADENCE, AND `metric_time` IS THEREFORE A CONVENTION WITH A UNIQUE OVER IT. §4.8 asks for "unique (published_post_id,metric_time)" and batch 121 writes it, but the Product Owner's answer to question F makes `metric_time` the provider's measurement instant TRUNCATED BY THE SERVICE to the collection cadence before the insert. No column on this table holds a cadence and no constraint could check one: an hourly collector and a daily collector satisfy every rule the table has. Two collectors running at different cadences against one post would interleave readings that look like one series and are not.

What IS enforced is that a re-collection at an instant already recorded is refused 23505 by performance_snapshots_one_per_post_instant rather than overwriting -- §4.8's "no destructive overwrite" -- and the fixture probes it. The cadence itself is owed to the command surface, and the fixture's instants are written on the hour so that what the rule looks like when obeyed is at least visible.

NOTHING HOLDS A METRIC SNAPSHOT TO BE NO OLDER THAN THE POST IT MEASURES. `metric_time >= app.published_posts.published_at` is a cross-table rule and a CHECK constraint cannot read another row, which is the sentence batch 120 wrote about a pinned asset version being `ready` and batch 100 wrote before it. A snapshot dated before its own publication is accepted by every layer this batch has. It is an integrity gap and not a leak -- the row is still confined to its post's tenant by performance_snapshots_post_scope_fk -- and it is recorded rather than left to look closed. Owed to the command surface.

§4.8 ASKS FOR A HIGH-VOLUME IDENTITY PK AND FOR PARTITION-READINESS BY MONTH, AND THE TWO CANNOT BOTH BE SATISFIED BY THIS TABLE AS BUILT. A PostgreSQL partitioned table requires every unique constraint, the primary key included, to CONTAIN the partition key. `performance_snapshots_one_per_post_instant unique (published_post_id, metric_time)` already does. `primary key (id)` does NOT, and the Product Owner's answer to question C takes "high-volume identity PK" literally, so the key is `id` alone.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED FOR THE BATCH THAT WILL MEET IT: the day batch 150 -- which §6's registry gives "indexes/partition readiness" -- declares `partition by range (metric_time)`, it will have to make the key `(id, metric_time)`, and on an existing table that is a REBUILD and not an `alter`. Batch 121 is partition-READY in the two senses it can deliver (the unique carries the partition column; the index prunes on it) and is not partition-ready in the sense that matters most to a table expected to be the largest in the schema. Nothing in 121 claims otherwise and its apply-time block asserts only what is true. Owed to batch 150. BATCH 150's PREREQUISITES (2026-10-04, plan a0-batch-150-prereq-plan-2026-10-03.md): db/foundation/lint/pinned-shapes.json now holds today's `PRIMARY KEY (id)` and every constraint, index and policy of app.performance_snapshots by text, so the rebuild this entry predicts rewrites that file in the same diff. Whether to make the key `(id, metric_time)` now, without declaring partitioning, is Q150-a (Owner), UNANSWERED; A0 recommends yes, as a small forward migration. The shapes pin no column (type, NOT NULL, default, identity), so a rebuild that changed `id`'s identity or `metric_time`'s nullability passes them: owed to A0 with Q150-a (open_blockers[194] (4)). CLOSED 2026-10-04 BY BATCH 150 (plan a0-batch-150-plan-2026-10-03.md; Q150-a answered yes by the Owner's `เิาตามแนะนำ` (2026-10-04, product-owner-disposition-2026-10-03-batch-150.md)): db/foundation/migrations/150_performance_snapshots_key.sql makes the key PRIMARY KEY (id, metric_time) by a forward migration under lock and statement timeouts, id still `generated always as identity`, after measuring on a clean migrate-clean of 1930f41 that no foreign key in any schema references app.performance_snapshots and that no unique, index, policy, trigger, grant or apply-time block names the key's columns (121's block is re-run unchanged by the post-migrate pass); db/foundation/lint/pinned-shapes.json is rewritten in the same diff; every unique now carries metric_time, so a monthly partition becomes a parent plus ATTACH, not a rebuild. NOT partitioned: Q150-b (answered: defer `partition by` and production index work until a production-like fixture and an SLO exist) owes that to batch 150's later part, which has no date. The columns half of the pin (F7) stays on open_blockers[194] (4). REVIEW ROUND (2026-10-04, plan a0-batch-150-plan-2026-10-03.md §11; C0-1 MEDIUM, re-measured by A0 on PostgreSQL 17.11, rolled back): THE CLOSED TEXT'S "a monthly partition becomes a parent plus ATTACH, not a rebuild" IS FALSE AS A MECHANISM. Attaching app.performance_snapshots to a range-partitioned parent is refused, 'table "performance_snapshots" being attached contains an identity column "id"' / 'The new partition may not contain an identity column', whether or not the parent's id is an identity. The path the server accepts, measured with 121's 4 fixture rows: drop the identity on the table's id (catalog only, no rewrite), create the parent with id generated always as identity and the key (id, metric_time), attach, restart the parent's identity above max(id) (all 4 rows read through the parent; the attached partition then reads attidentity 'a', the parent's). So no rewrite is still true and the re-key is still the necessary step; what is not true is 'attach alone'. 150's header, key comment, catalog table comment and block hint now say so (150 is not integrated, so it was edited in place). The batch that partitions also moves policies, grants and comments to the parent and supersedes 150's block (check 3 refuses a partition by design) and whatever of 121's block it no longer satisfies: that IDENTITY AND ATTACH HALF IS OPEN, owed to batch 150's later part (open_blockers[194] (2)), not designed here. The key half stays CLOSED. C0-7: '121's block names no key column' should read 'names no property 150 changes' (it holds id's identity, block 10, and metric_time's NOT NULL).

THE CORE ERD AND THE TABLE BLUEPRINT NAME THIS TABLE DIFFERENTLY, AND BATCH 121 HAD TO CHOOSE. §4 of the ERD document draws the entity as `METRIC_SNAPSHOT` ("PUBLISHED_POST ||--o{ METRIC_SNAPSHOT : measures"); §4.8 of the workstream document heads the bullet `performance_snapshots` and is the only one of the two that gives columns. Batch 121 takes §4.8, on the Product Owner's answer to question A and on the ground that §4 names an ENTITY while §4.8 names a TABLE. The isolation cases and the CI negative control nevertheless say `metric-snapshot`, because that is the family word a reader recognises and because `[a-z0-9-]*performance-snapshot` would have been a worse pattern beside batch 070's `research-snapshot`. A later reader therefore meets both names and should not conclude that one of them is a second table. Owed to whoever reconciles the two documents.

§8.6's CASE 4 CANNOT BE WRITTEN FOR app.performance_snapshots IN THE DIRECTION IT ASKS FOR, AND WHAT STANDS IN ITS PLACE IS A WEAKER MEASUREMENT. The case asks for a member allowed Page A to be refused a row on Page B. Every app.published_posts row in the fixture hangs off a BUSINESS-LEVEL content item, so there is no page-level metric to be refused: the two page-pinned rows in this family are an intent with no send and a send with no post, and both absences are load-bearing for three of batch 120's own service cases -- giving either one a post would turn a landing insert into a 23505, which is the mistake batch 120 recorded against itself.

What IS measured, and it contradicted batch 121's plan: `pinned-editor-a-sees-the-metric-snapshots-of-the-fb-send` returns two rows. §3.3 NAMES `social_account_id` AS A REQUIRED FIELD FOR METRICS AND app.performance_snapshots HAS NO SUCH COLUMN. A MAGNITUDE BOUND ON `metrics` VALUES IS A0's NUMBER AND NOT THE OWNER'S. CLOSED IN THIS BATCH by performance_snapshots_metrics_values_are_plausible, which requires every value to be between 0 and 10^12, with an apply-time probe writing A1's exact literal and demanding 23514 by name. A1 GRADED ITS OWN MANDATE'S PRE-DECLARED SEVERITY DOWN, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY THE AUTHOR. If the Owner reads §9.1's "external post ID" as making any admissible representation of one stop-the-line, then batch 121 was stop-the-line at head 426c294 and the record should say so even though the code is now fixed. The list to change is in three places in `121_publisher_metrics.sql`, one in the fixture, and `metrics_schema_version` exists precisely so an old row can say which set of rules it was written under. Owed to whoever adds a metric.

Two classes have no such probe. (1) FOREIGN DATA: A1 measured (r7) a loopback postgres_fdw server, user mapping and foreign table whose remote table is app.audit_logs, every statement computed in a DO block, migrating clean with every layer green; app_command, refused a direct insert, wrote a forged row through it, because the remote session is the migrating superuser and bypasses forced RLS and every policy. The same foreign table onto any app table is an RLS bypass for any non-client role granted it (app_command, app_worker, app_maintenance); the only probe that reads foreign tables, CLIENT_PRIVILEGE_PROBE_SQL, reads them for the client roles only. (2) FUNCTION LANGUAGE: A0 measured (s6) an internal function aliasing int4pl and a c function on pgcrypto's pg_digest that is no extension member, the language word computed, migrating clean with every probe green; the driver's own comment says such a function can alias any built-in, a server-file function included, under a name no list holds. Neither class is in any migration in the tree; each needs a migration written to evade the driver. OWED, independently of RFC-2026-026's approval: a catalog probe in run.mjs, with a self-test drift each, refusing after migrate-clean any pg_extension row outside APPROVED_EXTENSIONS plus plpgsql, any row of pg_foreign_data_wrapper, pg_foreign_server, pg_user_mapping or pg_foreign_table, and any function in a non-system schema in a language other than sql or plpgsql that is not a c member of an approved extension, each against a pinned exemption list (empty today) in a diff a reviewer reads.
